al-aziz.s: Al-Aziz is a name borne by two different rulers mentioned on the site. In the Fatimid Caliphate, al-Aziz Billah was the caliph who reigned from 975 to 996 and expanded Fatimid influence in Syria.

al-aziz-billah.s: Al-Aziz Billah was the fifth Fatimid caliph and the first to begin his reign in Egypt, ruling from 975 to 996. He extended Fatimid power in Syria and built up the army by recruiting Turkish and other troops alongside the Berber forces.

aztec-empire.s: The Aztec Empire was the Triple Alliance of Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan, formed in 1428 in the Valley of Mexico and dominated by the Mexica of Tenochtitlan. It collected tribute from a large number of subject city-states across central Mexico.

aztec-purepecha-war-of-1479.s: The Aztec–Purépecha war of 1479 was a military campaign by the Aztec ruler Axayacatl against the Purépecha (Tarascan) kingdom to the west. The Aztec army suffered a heavy defeat.

al-bakri.s: Al-Bakri was an Andalusian geographer and historian who wrote a description of North and West Africa completed around c. 1067.

al-kamil.s: Al-Kamil was an Ayyubid sultan of Egypt who reigned from 1218 to 1238, a nephew of Saladin. He promoted trade with Italian city-states.

al-khwarizmi.s: Al-Khwarizmi was a Persian mathematician, astronomer and geographer who worked in Baghdad during the Abbasid Caliphate in the ninth century. His treatise on calculation by completion and balancing gave algebra its name, and the word algorithm derives from his name.

al-kitab-al-mukhtasar-fi-hisab-al-jabr-w.n: Al-Kitāb al-mukhtaṣar fī ḥisāb al-jabr wal-muqābala
al-kitab-al-mukhtasar-fi-hisab-al-jabr-w.s: Al-Kitab al-mukhtasar fi hisab al-jabr wal-muqabala, the Compendious Book on Calculation by Completion and Balancing, is a mathematical treatise by al-Khwarizmi written in Baghdad around 820 CE. It set out systematic methods for solving linear and quadratic equations, and the…

al-mamun.s: Al-Mamun was an Abbasid caliph who reigned from 813 to 833. He came to power after a civil war against his brother al-Amin.

al-mansur-abbasid-caliph.s: Al-Mansur was the second Abbasid caliph, reigning from 754 to 775. He consolidated the new dynasty's power, eliminating rivals and building a centralised administration.

al-mustansir-billah.s: Al-Mustansir Billah was an Abbasid caliph of Baghdad in the thirteenth century. In 1229 he issued a formal investiture to Iltutmish, recognising him as Sultan of Hindustan and the legitimate Muslim sovereign in South Asia.

al-mustasim.s: Al-Musta'sim was the last Abbasid caliph to rule from Baghdad. When Mongol forces under Hulagu Khan captured the city in February 1258, he was executed and the House of Wisdom was destroyed.

al-mutasim.s: Al-Mu'tasim was an Abbasid caliph who reigned from 833 to 842. He created a standing army of Turkic slave soldiers, or ghilman, and moved the court to the new city of Samarra.

al-nasir-abbasid-caliph.s: Al-Nasir was an Abbasid caliph who reigned from 1180 to 1225. He sought to restore the political power of the caliphate in Iraq after a long period of domination by Seljuk sultans, using diplomacy and religious networks.

al-nasir-muhammad.s: Al-Nasir Muhammad was a sultan of the Mamluk Sultanate whose main reign lasted from 1310 to 1341. Under him the Mamluk state reached its institutional apex, with systematic allocation of iqta land grants, administrative reforms and extensive building in Cairo.

al-qaim.s: Al-Qa'im was an Abbasid caliph of the eleventh century whose authority was dominated first by the Shi'a Buyids. In 1055 the Seljuk leader Tughril entered Baghdad and freed him from Buyid control.

al-umari.s: Al-Umari was a fourteenth-century Arab historian and administrator in Mamluk Egypt and Syria, author of an encyclopaedic work on geography and administration. His writings are an important source on African states, including Mali and Ethiopia.

al-walid-i.s: Al-Walid I was an Umayyad caliph who reigned from 705 to 715. His reign saw the greatest expansion of the Umayyad Caliphate, including the conquests of Hispania, Sind and Transoxiana.

al-zubayr-rahma-mansur.s: Al-Zubayr Rahma Mansur was a Sudanese slave-trading merchant and warlord of the nineteenth century who built a powerful private army in the Bahr al-Ghazal region. Operating with tacit Egyptian backing, he invaded Darfur in 1874.

abd-al-rahman-iii.s: Abd al-Rahman III was the Umayyad emir of Córdoba from 912 who proclaimed himself caliph in 929, founding the Caliphate of Córdoba. He subdued rebels such as the Hafsunids of Bobastro, the Banu Qasi and the lords of Seville, reuniting al-Andalus, and fought the Christian…

azzone-visconti.s: Azzone Visconti was lord of Milan from 1329 to 1339. He bought the title of imperial vicar, rebuilt Milan's walls and public buildings, and extended Visconti rule over the neighbouring communes of Lombardy, including Bergamo, Como, Cremona, Lodi, Novara, Vercelli, Brescia and…

alexander-nevsky.s: Alexander Nevsky was a Rus' prince who served as prince of Novgorod and from 1252 as Grand Prince of Vladimir. He defeated the Swedes on the Neva in 1240 and the knights of the Livonian Order on the ice of Lake Peipus in 1242.

ahmad-shah-qajar.s: Ahmad Shah Qajar was the last shah of the Qajar dynasty of Iran, coming to the throne as a boy in 1909 after his father was deposed in the Constitutional Revolution. His weak reign saw foreign occupation during the First World War and Reza Khan's coup of 1921.

ahmad-shah-i-wali.s: Ahmad Shah I Wali was sultan of the Bahmani Sultanate of the Deccan from 1422 to 1436. He fought Vijayanagara, Warangal and Malwa, and moved the capital from Gulbarga to Bidar, which he rebuilt.

ahmad-shah-i-of-gujarat.s: Ahmad Shah I was sultan of Gujarat from 1411 to 1442, grandson of the dynasty's founder Muzaffar Shah. In 1411 he founded the city of Ahmedabad on the Sabarmati river and made it his capital.

alexios-iii-angelos.s: Alexios III Angelos was Byzantine emperor from 1195, after blinding and deposing his brother Isaac II. His weak rule allowed provincial lords such as Leo Sgouros and Dobromir Chrysos to set up their own lordships.

alexios-iii-of-trebizond.s: Alexios III Megas Komnenos was emperor of Trebizond from 1349 to 1390. He restored order after years of civil war and kept the small empire safe by diplomacy, marrying his daughters to neighbouring Turkmen emirs, including Taceddin.

antonio-lopez-de-santa-anna.s: Antonio López de Santa Anna was a Mexican general and politician who dominated the country's affairs from the 1820s to the 1850s and served as president several times. He helped overthrow the empire of Agustín de Iturbide, presided over the centralist republic, lost Texas in…

abd-allah-ibn-al-zubayr.s: Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr was a son of the Companion al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam and a grandson of Abu Bakr. Refusing to recognise the Umayyad Yazid I, he held Mecca and after 683 was proclaimed caliph, recognised for a time across most of the Islamic world during the Second Fitna.

abd-allah-ibn-muhammad-emir-of-cordoba.n: Abd Allah ibn Muhammad (emir of Córdoba)
abd-allah-ibn-muhammad-emir-of-cordoba.s: Abd Allah ibn Muhammad was the Umayyad Emir of Córdoba from 888 to 912. His reign was the low point of the emirate: rebels such as Umar ibn Hafsun held much of the south, and Arab families such as the Banu Hajjaj of Seville ruled their cities as independent lords.

abd-allah-ibn-buluggin.s: Abd Allah ibn Buluggin was the last Zirid king of the Taifa of Granada, ruling from 1073 to 1090 while his brother Tamim held Málaga. Caught between Alfonso VI of Castile, to whom he paid tribute, and the Almoravids, he was deposed by Yusuf ibn Tashfin in 1090 and exiled to…

abd-allah-ibn-al-aftas.s: Abd Allah ibn al-Aftas, of Berber descent, was the founder of the Aftasid dynasty of the Taifa of Badajoz. Vizier to Sabur al-Saqlabi, ruler of the old Lower March around Mérida and Badajoz, he seized power after Sabur's death in 1022 and ruled until about 1045, fighting the…

albert-ii-prince-of-monaco.s: Albert II has been Sovereign Prince of Monaco since the death of his father Rainier III in 2005. A member of the Grimaldi family, he competed in bobsleigh at five Winter Olympics and is a member of the International Olympic Committee.

albert-ii-duke-of-saxony.s: Albert II was an Ascanian Duke of Saxony who ruled jointly with his brother John I and then John's sons until the partition of 1296, which gave him the lands around Wittenberg on the Elbe, the Duchy of Saxe-Wittenberg, while his nephews received Saxe-Lauenburg. A supporter of…

albert-ii-duke-of-mecklenburg.s: Albert II was the ruler of Mecklenburg from 1329. In 1348 Emperor Charles IV raised him and his brother John to the rank of dukes of the empire, and in 1352 the brothers divided their lands, John receiving Stargard.

albert-iv-duke-of-bavaria.s: Albert IV, called the Wise, was Duke of Bavaria-Munich from 1465. After the War of the Landshut Succession of 1503–1505 he reunited the divided Wittelsbach duchies into a single Duchy of Bavaria, and in 1506 he decreed primogeniture so that the land would not be partitioned…

albert-iv-count-of-tyrol.s: Albert IV was the last Count of Tyrol of the original line, named after Tyrol Castle near Merano. As advocate of the bishoprics of Trent and Brixen he greatly extended his power in the Adige and Inn valleys.

alfonso-ii-of-asturias.s: Alfonso II, called the Chaste, was King of Asturias from 791 to 842. He made Oviedo his capital, modelled his court and church on the Visigothic kingdom of Toledo, resisted repeated Umayyad raids and kept contact with Charlemagne.

alfonso-ii-of-aragon.s: Alfonso II was the son of Ramon Berenguer IV of Barcelona and Petronila of Aragon. He became Count of Barcelona in 1162 and King of Aragon in 1164, the first ruler to hold both by inheritance, uniting them in what became the Crown of Aragon.

alfonso-ii-deste.s: Alfonso II d'Este was the last Duke of Ferrara of the Este family, ruling from 1559 to 1597. His court was a centre of music and literature, home to the poet Torquato Tasso, whom he confined for seven years as insane, and to the singers of the concerto delle donne.

ammianus-marcellinus.s: Ammianus Marcellinus was a Greek-born Roman soldier and historian. His Latin history, of which the books covering 353 to 378 survive, is the main source for the reigns of Constantius II, Julian and Valens.

andries-hendrik-potgieter.s: Andries Hendrik Potgieter was a leader of the Great Trek of the Boer Voortrekkers from the Cape Colony. He fought the Ndebele of Mzilikazi in 1836–1837, led settlers at Winburg, founded Potchefstroom in 1838 and later moved to the far north, where he founded the Zoutpansberg…

andries-pretorius.s: Andries Pretorius was a Voortrekker leader who commanded the Boer force that defeated the Zulu army of Dingane at Blood River in December 1838, securing the Natalia Republic. After Britain annexed Natal he moved inland, led resistance to British rule north of the Orange River…

ashikaga-takauji.s: Ashikaga Takauji was a Japanese warrior who in 1333 turned against the Kamakura shogunate and helped Emperor Go-Daigo destroy it. Breaking with Go-Daigo's Kenmu Restoration, he took Kyoto in 1336, installed an emperor of the rival Northern Court and in 1338 became shogun,…

ashurnasirpal-ii.s: Ashurnasirpal II was King of Assyria from 883 to 859 BCE and one of the founders of the Neo-Assyrian Empire. In yearly campaigns he subdued the Aramaean states along the Euphrates and the Khabur and the highlands of Nairi and Zamua, and reached the Mediterranean, collecting…

adam-kok-iii.s: Adam Kok III was kaptein of the Philippolis Griqua from 1837. He sought British protection against Boer settlers, but after the creation of the Orange Free State his people lost much of their land.

agrippa-ii.s: Agrippa II was the last ruler of the Herodian dynasty, son of Herod Agrippa I. Rome gave him the kingdom of Chalcis in about 50 and later larger territories in the north of Palestine.

albert-the-bear.s: Albert the Bear was a prince of the Ascanian house who received the Northern March from Lothair III in 1134. He inherited Brandenburg from the Hevelli prince Pribislav-Henry and secured it in 1157, taking the title Margrave of Brandenburg.

alim-khan-of-kokand.s: Alim Khan was a ruler of the Ming dynasty of Kokand who took the title khan around 1800, turning the Kokand state into a khanate. He built a standing army that included Tajik mountain soldiers and conquered Tashkent in 1808 or 1809.

altan-khan.s: Altan Khan was leader of the Tümed Mongols, a grandson of Dayan Khan who raided Ming China for decades. In 1571 he made peace with the Ming, gaining trade and a royal title, and he founded the city of Hohhot.

amanullah-khan.s: Amanullah Khan ruled Afghanistan from 1919 to 1929, first as emir and from 1926 as king. He fought the Third Anglo-Afghan War in 1919 and won full control of foreign policy from Britain.

andrei-bogolyubsky.s: Andrei Bogolyubsky was the son of Yuri Dolgoruky and Grand Prince of Vladimir from 1157. He moved his capital from Rostov-Suzdal to Vladimir, adorned it with white-stone churches and built a palace at Bogolyubovo.

aslan-khan-of-kazikumukh.s: Aslan Khan was a member of the ruling family of the Kazikumukh Khanate in Dagestan and a loyal ally of the Russian Empire in the early 19th century. The Russians placed the newly formed Kurin Khanate, with its seat at Kurakh, under him, and he later also ruled Kazikumukh.

aung-san.s: Aung San was a Burmese nationalist leader who founded the Burma Independence Army with Japanese help in 1941. He led the army of the Japanese-sponsored State of Burma but turned it against Japan in 1945.

aydinoglu-mehmed-bey.s: Aydınoğlu Mehmed Bey was a commander in the service of the Germiyanids who founded the Aydinid beylik in western Anatolia around 1308. He conquered Birgi, which became his capital, Ayasoluk (Ephesus) and the upper citadel of Smyrna.

al-rashid-of-morocco.s: Al-Rashid was the first sultan of the Alaouite dynasty of Morocco, ruling from 1666 to 1672. Starting from the Tafilalt, he took Fez in 1666, crushed the Dila'iyya in 1668, took the corsair towns of Salé and Rabat, captured Marrakesh in 1669 and subdued Tazeroualt in 1670,…

abd-al-aziz-ibn-abi-amir.s: Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Amir, a grandson of the Córdoban regent al-Mansur, ruled the taifa of Valencia from 1021 to 1061. He was recognised by the city after the collapse of the Caliphate of Córdoba and for a time also held Almería.

abd-al-karim-qasim.s: Abd al-Karim Qasim was an Iraqi army officer who led the revolution of 14 July 1958 that overthrew the Hashemite monarchy. As prime minister of the new republic he carried out land reform and left the Baghdad Pact.

abdullah-al-salim-al-sabah.s: Abdullah Al-Salim Al-Sabah was ruler of Kuwait from 1950 until his death in 1965. Oil revenues under his rule paid for schools, hospitals and housing.

abeid-karume.s: Abeid Karume was leader of the Afro-Shirazi Party and became President of Zanzibar after the revolution of January 1964 overthrew the sultan. In April 1964 he agreed with Julius Nyerere to unite Zanzibar with Tanganyika as Tanzania, becoming its first vice-president while…

abu-hafs-umar-al-hintati.s: Abu Hafs Umar al-Hintati was a Masmuda Berber chief and one of the first companions of Ibn Tumart, founder of the Almohad movement. He became a leading commander and adviser of the Almohad caliphs.

abu-hafs-umar-al-iqritishi.s: Abu Hafs Umar al-Iqritishi led the Andalusi exiles who had rebelled against the Umayyad emir of Córdoba and later held Alexandria. Forced out of Egypt, he landed on Byzantine Crete in the 820s, conquered the island and founded the Emirate of Crete with its capital at Chandax,…

adam-kok-ii.s: Adam Kok II was a Griqua kaptein in southern Africa. He led the community at Griquatown alongside Barend Barends until a split in the 1820s, then moved with his followers to Philippolis, north of the Orange River, which became the centre of a separate Griqua state.

adolf-hitler.s: Adolf Hitler was the leader of the Nazi Party and dictator of Germany from 1933 to 1945. Appointed chancellor of the Weimar Republic in January 1933, he quickly abolished democracy and built a totalitarian state.

adolphe-thiers.s: Adolphe Thiers was a French historian and statesman who served as a minister and prime minister under the July Monarchy. After the defeat by Prussia he became head of the executive in 1871, made peace and sent the army to crush the Paris Commune in May 1871.

adud-al-dawla.s: Adud al-Dawla was the greatest ruler of the Buyid dynasty. Emir of Fars from 949, he took over Iraq and Baghdad in 978, defeated his rivals and made the Hamdanids of Mosul and other neighbours submit, uniting most Buyid lands under his rule.

ahmad-ibn-abd-al-aziz-ibn-abi-dulaf.n: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Dulaf
ahmad-ibn-abd-al-aziz-ibn-abi-dulaf.s: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Aziz was the most notable ruler of the Dulafid dynasty, which governed the region of Jibal in western Iran under the Abbasid caliphs. He fought the Saffarids and at times defied Baghdad.

ahmad-simba.s: Ahmad Simba was a Nabhani prince of Pate who fled the Sultanate of Zanzibar's control and founded the sultanate of Witu on the Kenyan coast in the 1860s. His state took in runaway slaves and farmers.

al-ashraf-musa-sultan-of-damascus.s: Al-Ashraf Musa was an Ayyubid prince, son of al-Adil, who ruled the Jazira from Harran and later became Sultan of Damascus in 1229. In 1230 he took Baalbek from its emir Bahramshah.

al-ashraf-musa-emir-of-homs.s: Al-Ashraf Musa was the last Ayyubid emir of Homs. He lost the city in 1248 to al-Nasir Yusuf of Aleppo, who gave him Tell Bashir instead.

albert-of-brandenburg.s: Albert of Brandenburg was a Hohenzollern prince who became Archbishop of Magdeburg, administrator of Halberstadt and, in 1514, Archbishop-Elector of Mainz, and was made a cardinal in 1518. To pay the debts from acquiring these sees he promoted the sale of indulgences, which…

albigensian-crusade.s: The Albigensian Crusade was a war called by Pope Innocent III against the Cathar heretics of Languedoc and the lords who protected them, chiefly the Count of Toulouse. Northern French barons under Simon de Montfort took Béziers and Carcassonne in 1209.

albrecht-von-wallenstein.s: Albrecht von Wallenstein was a Bohemian nobleman who raised and commanded the imperial armies in the Thirty Years' War. Rewarded with the duchies of Friedland, Sagan and, in 1628, Mecklenburg, he became one of the most powerful men in the Empire.

alexandros-mavrokordatos.s: Alexandros Mavrokordatos was a Phanariote Greek statesman of the Greek War of Independence. In 1821 he organised the provisional administration of Western Continental Greece, and in 1822 he became president of the executive of the First Hellenic Republic.

alexandru-ioan-cuza.s: Alexandru Ioan Cuza was elected Prince of Moldavia and then of Wallachia in 1859, uniting the two principalities in a personal union that became Romania. He carried out land reform, secularised monastery estates and introduced compulsory primary education.

alfonso-iii-of-asturias.s: Alfonso III, called the Great, was King of Asturias from 866 to 910. His vassals took Porto in 868 and Coimbra in 878, extending Christian settlement to the Douro and Mondego and creating the counties of Portugal and Coimbra.

alfonso-vii-of-leon-and-castile.n: Alfonso VII of León and Castile
alfonso-vii-of-leon-and-castile.s: Alfonso VII was King of León and Castile from 1126 and was crowned Emperor of All Spain in 1135. He exploited the collapse of Almoravid power to intervene in the second taifas, made Muslim rulers his vassals and in 1147 captured Almería with Genoese and Catalan help.

alfonso-xii.s: Alfonso XII was King of Spain from 1874 to 1885. Son of Isabella II, he was proclaimed king by a military coup in December 1874, ending the First Republic and beginning the Restoration.

ali-abdullah-saleh.s: Ali Abdullah Saleh was President of North Yemen from 1978 and, after unification in 1990, the first President of the Republic of Yemen. He won the civil war of 1994 against southern separatists.

ali-ibn-muhammad-zanj-leader.s: Ali ibn Muhammad was the leader of the Zanj Rebellion in southern Iraq. In 869 he raised the enslaved East Africans who worked the salt marshes around Basra, claiming descent from Ali and promising them freedom.

ali-ibn-muhammad-al-sulayhi.s: Ali ibn Muhammad al-Sulayhi was the founder of the Sulayhid dynasty in Yemen, which ruled in the name of the Fatimid caliphs of Cairo. Proclaiming Ismaili rule in 1047, he conquered most of Yemen including Zabid and Sana'a and extended influence to Mecca.

al-nasir-yusuf.s: An-Nasir Yusuf was the last major Ayyubid ruler in Syria, Sultan of Aleppo from 1236 and of Damascus from 1250. He reunited much of Ayyubid Syria but failed to recover Egypt from the Mamluks.

american-revolutionary-war.s: The American Revolutionary War was fought between Britain and its rebel colonies in North America, which declared independence as the United States in 1776. France, Spain and the Dutch Republic joined against Britain, and German states such as Hesse-Kassel and Ansbach hired…

amir-husayn.s: Amir Husayn was the leader of the Qara'unas, grandson of Qazaghan, who dominated the Western Chagatai Khanate in the 1360s. He allied with Timur against the Moghuls of the eastern khanate, but the two became rivals.

andres-de-santa-cruz.s: Andrés de Santa Cruz was President of Bolivia from 1829 to 1839. In 1836 he joined Bolivia with the North and South Peruvian republics in the Peru–Bolivian Confederation, taking the title of Supreme Protector.

antanas-smetona.s: Antanas Smetona was the first President of Lithuania, from 1919 to 1920, and returned to power after the military coup of December 1926. He ruled as an authoritarian leader of the Nationalist Union until the Soviet ultimatum of June 1940, when he fled abroad.

apolinario-mabini.s: Apolinario Mabini was a Filipino lawyer and political thinker who became the chief adviser of Emilio Aguinaldo in 1898, despite being paralysed. He drafted decrees for the revolutionary government and served as the first prime minister of the First Philippine Republic in 1899.

arya-penangsang.s: Arya Penangsang was the ruler of Jipang, a nephew line of the Demak royal house in Java, who claimed the throne in the succession war after Sultan Trenggana's death in 1546. He had his rivals Sunan Prawoto and the husband of Ratu Kalinyamat killed.

ashikaga-yoshimitsu.s: Ashikaga Yoshimitsu was the third shogun of the Ashikaga shogunate, from 1368 to 1394. He reunited the Northern and Southern Courts in 1392, curbed powerful provincial lords such as the Ōuchi in 1399 and opened official trade with Ming China.

askar-akayev.s: Askar Akayev is a Kyrgyz physicist who was elected president of the Kirghiz SSR in 1990 and led Kyrgyzstan to independence in 1991. Seen at first as a reformer, he became increasingly authoritarian.

abul-abbas-mamun.s: Abu'l-Abbas Ma'mun, Ma'mun II, was Khwarazmshah of the Ma'munid dynasty from 1009 to 1017, ruling from Gurganj. He continued his brother Ali's patronage of scholars, among them al-Biruni and, for a time, Ibn Sina.

al-qasim-ibn-muhammad.s: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad was a Zaydi scholar who proclaimed himself imam in the northern highlands of Yemen in 1597 and launched a revolt against Ottoman rule. He fought until a truce in 1619.

abba-bagibo.s: Abba Bagibo was king of Limmu-Ennarea, the leading Oromo monarchy of the Gibe region in south-western Ethiopia, in the first half of the 19th century. Under him the kingdom reached its height as a market for gold, ivory, civet and slaves, with trade links to Gojjam and the coast.

abba-jifar-ii.s: Abba Jifar II was king of Jimma, the richest of the Oromo Gibe kingdoms, from 1878 to 1932. In 1882 he submitted to Menelik II and paid tribute, which allowed Jimma to keep its internal autonomy, and he helped bring neighbouring Janjero under Ethiopian rule.

abd-al-rahman-ibn-rustam.s: Abd al-Rahman ibn Rustam was an Ibadi leader of Persian descent who governed Kairouan for the Ibadi Imamate of Tripolitania from 758. After the Abbasids defeated the Ibadis in 761 he fled west and founded Tahert in the central Maghreb, where around 777 he was recognised as imam.

abd-al-rahman-ii.s: Abd al-Rahman II was Umayyad emir of Córdoba from 822 to 852. He reorganised the administration on Abbasid lines, enlarged the Great Mosque of Córdoba and welcomed the musician Ziryab, who brought Baghdad fashions to al-Andalus.

abd-el-krim.s: Abd el-Krim was a Riffian Berber judge and leader who led the tribes of northern Morocco against Spanish rule. In 1921 his forces destroyed a Spanish army at Annual, and he proclaimed the Rif Republic.

abdallah-jamma.s: Abdallah Jamma was the leader of the Qawasma Arabs on the middle Nile around 1500. In alliance with the Funj leader Amara Dunqas he destroyed the Christian kingdom of Alodia and its capital Soba.

abdul-kader-kan.s: Abdul Kader Kan was a Fula Muslim scholar who led the clerical revolution in Futa Toro, on the middle Senegal River, against the Denianke dynasty. In 1776 he became the first almamy of the Imamate of Futa Toro, an elected Islamic ruler.

abdullah-al-sallal.s: Abdullah al-Sallal was a Yemeni army officer who led the coup of 26 September 1962 that overthrew Imam Muhammad al-Badr and ended the Mutawakkilite Kingdom. He became the first president of the Yemen Arab Republic and relied heavily on Egyptian troops in the civil war against…

abdur-rahman-khan.s: Abdur Rahman Khan, the 'Iron Emir', ruled Afghanistan from 1880 to 1901 after the Second Anglo-Afghan War. With British subsidies and control of his foreign policy, he built a standing army, crushed tribal revolts, annexed Badakhshan and the Hazarajat and forcibly converted…

abu-bakar-of-johor.s: Abu Bakar of Johor was temenggung of Johor from 1862, maharaja from 1868 and sultan from 1886. He moved his capital to Johor Bahru, encouraged Chinese pepper and gambier planters, and travelled to Europe, cultivating Queen Victoria and the British.

abu-fudayk.s: Abu Fudayk, Abd Allah ibn Thawr, was a Kharijite leader of the Najdiyya movement in eastern Arabia. Around 691 the movement's followers deposed and killed their leader Najda ibn Amir and turned to him, and he ruled from Bahrain.

abu-qurra.s: Abu Qurra was the leader of the Banu Ifran, a Zenata Berber tribe of the central Maghreb, during the Berber revolts against Arab rule. A Sufri Kharijite, he was proclaimed imam at Tlemcen around 742 and founded the first Ifranid state.

abu-zakariya-yahya-i.s: Abu Zakariya Yahya I was the founder of the Hafsid Sultanate of Tunis. Governor of Ifriqiya for the Almohads, he broke with Marrakesh in 1229 and declared independence.

act-of-union-1840.s: The Act of Union 1840 was a British statute that merged Upper Canada and Lower Canada into the single Province of Canada, proclaimed in February 1841. It followed the rebellions of 1837 and 1838 and Lord Durham's report, which aimed to assimilate French Canadians.

adarnase-iv-of-iberia.s: Adarnase IV of Iberia was a Bagratid prince of Tao-Klarjeti in south-western Georgia. In 888 he took the title king of the Iberians, restoring Georgian kingship after about three centuries, and ruled until 923.

aden-abdullah-osman.s: Aden Abdullah Osman, known as Aden Adde, was the first president of Somalia. A leader of the Somali Youth League, he became president when the Trust Territory of Somaliland and the State of Somaliland united as the Somali Republic on 1 July 1960.

adil-shahi-dynasty.s: The Adil Shahi dynasty ruled the Bijapur Sultanate in the western Deccan from 1490, when Yusuf Adil Shah broke away from the Bahmani Sultanate, until the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb took Bijapur in 1686. Its sultans built the Gol Gumbaz and other monuments.

adolf-frederick-king-of-sweden.s: Adolf Frederick, King of Sweden, was a prince of the house of Holstein-Gottorp who served as prince-bishop of Lübeck from 1727 to 1750. Chosen heir to the Swedish throne in 1743 under Russian pressure, he became king in 1751.

adolf-frederick-i-duke-of-mecklenburg.n: Adolf Frederick I, Duke of Mecklenburg
adolf-frederick-i-duke-of-mecklenburg.s: Adolf Frederick I, Duke of Mecklenburg, shared the duchy with his brother John Albert II and divided it with him in 1621, taking Mecklenburg-Schwerin while John Albert received Mecklenburg-Güstrow. During the Thirty Years' War both brothers were deposed by the emperor in…

adolf-frederick-ii-of-mecklenburg-streli.s: Adolf Frederick II of Mecklenburg-Strelitz was the first duke of Mecklenburg-Strelitz. After a long succession dispute in the Mecklenburg house, the Treaty of Hamburg of 1701 gave him the eastern Stargard lands and the Principality of Ratzeburg as a separate duchy.

aeolians.s: The Aeolians were one of the main divisions of the ancient Greeks, speaking the Aeolic dialect, at home in Thessaly and Boeotia. Around 1000 BCE Aeolian settlers crossed the Aegean to Lesbos and the north-west coast of Anatolia, founding cities such as Mytilene, Cyme and Old…

agathocles-of-syracuse.s: Agathocles of Syracuse seized power as tyrant of Syracuse in 317 BCE and later took the title of king. Fighting Carthage for control of Sicily, he boldly invaded North Africa in 310 BCE.

agueybana-ii.s: Agüeybaná II was a Taíno cacique of Puerto Rico, successor to his brother Agüeybaná I as leading chief of the island. In 1511, after the Taíno learned that the Spaniards were not immortal, he led a general uprising against forced labour under the encomienda system.

agustin-gamarra.s: Agustín Gamarra was a Peruvian general and president from 1829 to 1833 and again from 1838 to 1841. A leading opponent of Andrés de Santa Cruz, he was defeated by him in 1835 and fought the Peru-Bolivian Confederation from exile with Chilean support.

ah-dzun-xiu.s: Ah Dzun Xiu was the lord of the Xiu lineage of Maní in northern Yucatán. In 1536 he led an embassy to make offerings at the sacred cenote of Chichen Itza, and on the way the party was murdered at Otzmal by Nachi Cocom of Sotuta.

ahmad-jalayir.s: Ahmad Jalayir was the Jalayirid sultan of Baghdad and Tabriz from 1382 to 1410, a poet, calligrapher and patron of manuscript painting. Timur drove him from Baghdad in 1393 and 1401, and he took refuge with the Mamluks and the Ottomans before returning.

ahmad-pasha-of-baghdad.s: Ahmad Pasha of Baghdad succeeded his father Hasan Pasha as Ottoman governor of Baghdad in 1723 and ruled, with a short interruption, until 1747. He defended the city against Nader Shah's sieges in the 1730s and 1740s.

ahmad-yar-khan.s: Ahmad Yar Khan was the last ruling Khan of Kalat, from 1933 to 1955. At the end of British rule in 1947 he declared Kalat independent, but in March 1948 he acceded to Pakistan.

ahmed-bey-of-constantine.s: Ahmed Bey of Constantine was the last bey of the eastern province of Ottoman Algeria, from 1826. After the French took Algiers in 1830 he kept Constantine independent and repulsed a French assault in 1836.

ahmed-karamanli.s: Ahmed Karamanli was an Ottoman cavalry officer in Tripoli who seized power in 1711, killed the Janissary officers and founded the hereditary Karamanli dynasty of pashas. Recognised by the sultan, he ruled until 1745, extended his authority over Cyrenaica and Fezzan and drew…

ahmetjan-qasimi.s: Ahmetjan Qasimi was a Soviet-educated Uyghur leader of the Second East Turkestan Republic in the Ili region of Xinjiang. A secular leftist, he became its leading figure after Elihan Töre was removed in 1946 and served in the coalition government with the Nationalists.

akhmat-khan.s: Akhmat Khan was khan of the Great Horde, the main successor of the Golden Horde, from about 1465 to 1481. He demanded tribute from Moscow and allied with Poland-Lithuania against Ivan III.

aku-uka.s: Aku Uka is the title of the sacred king of the Jukun people of the Benue valley in Nigeria. The king's wellbeing was believed to be bound to rain and harvest, and he lived secluded from ordinary view, surrounded by ritual officials.

ala-al-din-ali.s: Ala al-Din Ali was the last effective ruler of the Eretnid sultanate of central Anatolia, grandson of its founder Eretna. He came to the throne as a boy in 1365 and his reign was troubled by revolts of emirs and Turkmen chiefs.

alban-hills.s: The Alban Hills are the remains of an extinct volcano about 20 kilometres south-east of Rome, with crater lakes such as Lake Albano and Lake Nemi. In Roman tradition they were the site of Alba Longa, the mother city of the Latins, and of the Latin festival on the Alban Mount.

albert-iii-duke-of-saxony.s: Albert III, Duke of Saxony, called the Bold, founded the Albertine line of the Wettin house when he and his brother Ernest divided Saxony in 1485. A leading general of Emperor Maximilian I, he was named hereditary governor of Friesland in 1498 and imposed Saxon rule on the…

alessandro-farnese-duke-of-parma.s: Alessandro Farnese, Duke of Parma, was the most famous general of Habsburg Spain in the Dutch Revolt. As governor of the Spanish Netherlands from 1578, he reconquered the southern provinces through diplomacy and siege, taking Antwerp in 1585.

alessandro-sforza.s: Alessandro Sforza was a condottiero and the younger brother of Francesco Sforza, Duke of Milan. In 1445 he bought Pesaro from Galeazzo Malatesta, whose granddaughter Costanza da Varano he had married, and he ruled it as papal vicar until his death.

alexander-bustamante.s: Alexander Bustamante was a Jamaican labour leader and politician who rose to prominence in the labour unrest of 1938. He founded the Bustamante Industrial Trade Union and the Jamaica Labour Party, and won the first election under universal suffrage in 1944.

alexander-filimonov.s: Alexander Filimonov was a Russian army officer and ataman of the Kuban Cossack Host from 1917 to 1919. During the Russian Civil War he headed the Kuban People's Republic and tried to balance its Rada, where a Ukrainian-minded faction sought federation with Ukraine, against the…

alexander-i-of-epirus.s: Alexander I of Epirus, called the Molossian, was king of the Molossians in Epirus and the brother-in-law and uncle of Alexander the Great. Invited by Taras to fight the Italic peoples of southern Italy, he campaigned against the Lucanians, Bruttii and Samnites from 334 BCE.

alexandros-zaimis.s: Alexandros Zaimis was a Greek statesman who served several times as prime minister. In 1906 he replaced Prince George as High Commissioner of the autonomous Cretan State, holding the post until 1911 as the island moved towards union with Greece.

alexius-slav.s: Alexius Slav was a Bulgarian noble, a relative of the Asen tsars, who after Tsar Kaloyan's death in 1207 refused to accept Boril and set up his own principality in the Rhodope mountains. Ruling from Melnik with the title of despot, he allied with the Latin Empire and married a…

alfonso-xiii.s: Alfonso XIII was king of Spain from his birth in 1886 until 1931. His reign followed the loss of the last colonies in 1898 and saw the costly war in Morocco and the disaster at Annual in 1921, and growing labour unrest.

alfred-the-great.s: Alfred the Great was king of Wessex from 871 to 899. After defeating the Danish Great Heathen Army at Edington in 878, he built fortified burhs, reorganised the army and a fleet, and promoted learning and translation into English.

ali-bey-al-kabir.s: Ali Bey al-Kabir was a Mamluk bey of Georgian origin who became the dominant power in Ottoman Egypt in the 1760s. In 1768 he deposed the Ottoman governor and acted as an independent ruler, crushing the Hawwara of Upper Egypt and sending armies into the Hejaz and Syria.

ali-ibn-ghaniya.s: Ali ibn Ghaniya was a member of the Banu Ghaniya, the Almoravid family ruling the Balearic Islands. In 1184 he landed at Bejaia, seized it from the Almohad Caliphate and began a long war to restore Almoravid rule in Ifriqiya, recognising the Abbasid caliph and allying with…

ali-ibn-mahdi.s: Ali ibn Mahdi was a preacher from the Tihama, the coastal plain of Yemen, who denounced the luxury of the Najahid rulers of Zabid and gathered a following among the tribes from the 1130s. After years of raids he captured Zabid in 1159, ending the Najahid dynasty, and died the…

ali-mohammed-khan.s: Ali Mohammed Khan was the founder of Rohilla power in Rohilkhand, the region east of the upper Ganges. Adopted son of the Afghan chief Daud Khan, he built a following of Rohilla soldiers from the 1720s, made Aonla his capital and won recognition from the Mughal emperor.

ali-pasha-of-yanina.s: Ali Pasha of Yanina was an Albanian Ottoman governor who from 1788 ruled Epirus, southern Albania and much of mainland Greece from Ioannina. He built a near-independent state, dealt directly with Napoleon and Britain, and was visited by Lord Byron.

al-nasir-dawud.s: al-Nasir Dawud was an Ayyubid prince, son of al-Mu'azzam Isa. He briefly ruled Damascus from 1227 until his uncles took it in 1229, after which he held the fortress of Kerak east of the Dead Sea as his principality.

alphonse-count-of-poitiers.s: Alphonse, Count of Poitiers, was a brother of King Louis IX of France. He received Poitou as an appanage in 1241 and, through his marriage to Joan, heiress of Raymond VII, became count of Toulouse in 1249.

amadu-amadu.s: Amadu Amadu was the third and last ruler of the Massina Empire, the Fula Islamic state in the inner Niger delta, from 1853. Grandson of its founder Seku Amadu, he faced internal opposition and the rivalry of the Tijani leader Umar Tall.

amara-dunqas.s: Amara Dunqas was the first sultan of the Funj Sultanate, ruling from about 1504 to 1533. He founded Sennar on the Blue Nile, and together with Abdallah Jamma of the Qawasma Arabs he destroyed the Christian kingdom of Alodia.

american-civil-war.s: The American Civil War was fought between the United States and the eleven southern states that seceded as the Confederacy to defend slavery. The Union victory ended slavery and preserved the country.

american-revolution.s: The American Revolution was the rebellion of thirteen British colonies in North America, which declared independence in 1776 and won it in the war that ended with the Treaty of Paris in 1783. Most Iroquois nations sided with Britain and lost their lands, while tens of…

amir-khan-of-tonk.s: Amir Khan of Tonk was a Pathan soldier of fortune who led a large army of mercenary cavalry in central India, allied with Yashwant Rao Holkar and plundering Rajput states. In 1817, during the Pindari campaign, he agreed with the East India Company to disband his army in return…

anantavarman-chodaganga.s: Anantavarman Chodaganga was king of the Eastern Ganga dynasty, related to the Cholas through his mother. In a reign of about seventy years he conquered the Somavamshi kingdom and united the lands from the Ganges to the Godavari, moving his capital to Cuttack.

andre-rigaud.s: André Rigaud was a leader of the free people of colour in southern Saint-Domingue during the Haitian Revolution. He fought the British occupation in the 1790s but lost the War of the Knives against Toussaint Louverture in 1799–1800 and went into exile.

andriantsoly.s: Andriantsoly was the last independent Sakalava king of Boina in north-western Madagascar, a convert to Islam. When the Merina under Radama I took Mahajanga in 1824 he fled to the Comoros and later made himself ruler of Mayotte.

anglo-irish-treaty.s: The Anglo-Irish Treaty was signed in London on 6 December 1921 by British ministers and Irish delegates led by Arthur Griffith and Michael Collins, ending the Irish War of Independence. It created the Irish Free State as a self-governing dominion, with an oath of fidelity to…

antonio-jose-de-sucre.s: Antonio José de Sucre was a Venezuelan general and Simón Bolívar's closest lieutenant in the Spanish American wars of independence. He won the Battle of Pichincha in 1822, freeing Quito, and the decisive Battle of Ayacucho in 1824, which ended Spanish power in South America.

aq-sunqur-al-hajib.s: Aq Sunqur al-Hajib was a Turkish commander of the Seljuk sultan Malik-Shah I, appointed governor of Aleppo in 1087. He restored order and prosperity to northern Syria, but after Malik-Shah's death he turned against the Seljuk prince Tutush, who defeated and executed him in 1094.

arcesilaus-iv.s: Arcesilaus IV was the last king of the Battiad dynasty of Cyrene, the Greek city in Libya. His chariot victory at the Pythian Games at Delphi in 462 BCE was celebrated in two odes by Pindar.

arduin-of-ivrea.s: Arduin of Ivrea was margrave of Ivrea in north-western Italy who was elected King of Italy by Italian nobles in 1002, after the death of Emperor Otto III. Opposed by the bishops and by the German king Henry II, he held out until 1014, when he abdicated and retired to a monastery.

arnulf-of-carinthia.s: Arnulf of Carinthia was an illegitimate Carolingian who deposed his uncle Charles the Fat in 887 and became king of East Francia. He defeated the Vikings on the Dyle in 891, fought Great Moravia and was crowned emperor in Rome in 896.

arslan-shah-ibn-toghrul.s: Arslan Shah ibn Toghrul was sultan of the Seljuk Sultanate of Iraq from 1161 to 1176. His stepfather Eldiguz, the atabeg of Azerbaijan, placed him on the throne and held real power in his name.

ashikaga-yoshiaki.s: Ashikaga Yoshiaki was the fifteenth and last shogun of the Ashikaga shogunate. After his brother was murdered in 1565 he sought shelter with the Asakura and others, and in 1568 Oda Nobunaga marched into Kyoto and installed him as shogun.

ashot-i-of-iberia.s: Ashot I of Iberia was the Bagratid prince who established his family as the leading power in Georgia. Driven from Tbilisi by the Arabs, he moved to Tao-Klarjeti in the south-west early in the 9th century, rebuilt Artanuji and received the Byzantine title of kouropalates.

ashot-i-of-armenia.s: Ashot I of Armenia, called the Great, was a Bagratid prince recognised by the Abbasid caliph as prince of princes of Armenia in 862. In 884 or 885 he was crowned king with the consent of both the caliph and the Byzantine emperor, restoring the Armenian monarchy after more than…

augsburg-confession.s: The Augsburg Confession is the founding statement of Lutheran belief, drafted by Philip Melanchthon and presented to Emperor Charles V at the Diet of Augsburg in 1530. It was signed by several princes, including Wolfgang of Anhalt, and by the imperial cities of Nuremberg and…

auguste-pavie.s: Auguste Pavie was a French explorer and diplomat who mapped much of Laos and Cambodia. As French vice-consul at Luang Prabang, he rescued King Oun Kham when Chinese Haw raiders sacked the city in 1887, winning the loyalty of the court.

ayub-khan.s: Ayub Khan was a Pakistani general who became commander-in-chief in 1951 and seized power in the coup of October 1958, ruling as president until 1969. He introduced a new constitution with indirect elections, promoted rapid industrial growth and moved the capital to the new…

ayuka-khan.s: Ayuka Khan was ruler of the Kalmyks on the lower Volga from 1669 to 1724, the most powerful leader of the Kalmyk Khanate. He received the title of khan from the Dalai Lama, led wars against the Nogais, Kazakhs and Crimean Tatars and supplied cavalry to Russia under treaties…

albert-of-riga.s: Albert of Riga was a canon of Bremen who became bishop of Livonia in 1199 and led the crusade against the pagan peoples of the eastern Baltic. He founded Riga in 1201 and the military order of the Livonian Brothers of the Sword in 1202.

avicenna.s: Avicenna, Ibn Sina, was a Persian philosopher and physician born near Bukhara under the Samanids. His Canon of Medicine was a standard medical textbook in the Islamic world and Europe for centuries, and his Book of Healing shaped later philosophy.

adolf-of-nassau.s: Adolf of Nassau was a count of Nassau elected King of the Romans in 1292. To build support he granted and confirmed privileges to towns such as Sélestat and Leutkirch.

as-salih-ismail.s: As-Salih Ismail was an Ayyubid prince, son of al-Adil I, who held Baalbek and ruled Damascus briefly in 1237 and again from 1239 to 1245. In his rivalry with his nephew as-Salih Ayyub, sultan of Egypt, he allied with the Crusader states and ceded castles such as Beaufort to…

abba-magal.s: Abba Magal was an Oromo war leader remembered as the founder of the Kingdom of Jimma in the Gibe valley of south-western Ethiopia, around the beginning of the 19th century. The monarchy he established grew by absorbing neighbouring Oromo groups.

abd-al-aziz-al-bakri.s: Abd al-Aziz al-Bakri was the second and last ruler of the Taifa of Huelva and Saltés in south-western al-Andalus, a member of the Arab Bakri family. In 1051 the Abbadid ruler al-Mutadid of Seville forced him to give up his realm.

abd-al-aziz-ibn-musa.s: Abd al-Aziz ibn Musa was the son of Musa ibn Nusayr and the first Umayyad governor of al-Andalus, from 714 to 716. During the conquest of the Iberian peninsula he signed a treaty in 713 with the Visigothic noble Theodemir, leaving him seven towns in the south-east in return…

abd-al-aziz-ibn-mutib-al-rashid.n: Abd al-Aziz ibn Mutib Al Rashid
abd-al-aziz-ibn-mutib-al-rashid.s: Abd al-Aziz ibn Mutib Al Rashid was emir of Jabal Shammar, ruled from Ha'il, from 1897 to 1906. He inherited the dominant power in central Arabia from his uncle Muhammad ibn Rashid but lost Riyadh to Ibn Saud in 1902.

abd-al-aziz-ibn-shuayb.s: Abd al-Aziz ibn Shu'ayb was the last emir of the Emirate of Crete, ruling from about 949. In 960 the Byzantine general Nikephoros Phokas landed on the island and besieged its capital, Chandax, which fell in March 961.

abd-allah-al-bayyasi.s: Abd Allah al-Bayyasi was an Almohad prince and governor in al-Andalus who proclaimed himself caliph at Baeza in 1224, during the succession crisis after the death of the caliph Yusuf II. He sought the help of Ferdinand III of Castile against his rivals, ceding castles in…

abd-allah-al-murtada.s: Abd Allah al-Murtada was the governor of the Balearic Islands who declared himself independent at Madina Mayurqa, the later Palma, in 1076, when the Taifa of Dénia, which had ruled the islands, was annexed by Zaragoza. He ruled the Taifa of Majorca until his death around 1093,…

abd-allah-beg.s: Abd Allah Beg was the leader of the Kumul (Hami) oasis in eastern Xinjiang who submitted to the Kangxi Emperor of the Qing in 1696, as the Dzungar Khanate threatened the region. He helped Qing armies against the Dzungars and was rewarded with a hereditary rank.

abd-allah-ibn-ali-al-uyuni.s: Abd Allah ibn Ali al-Uyuni was a chief of the Abd al-Qays tribe who founded the Uyunid Emirate of eastern Arabia. In 1076 he rebelled against the Qarmatians of Bahrain and, with the help of a Seljuk army, took al-Ahsa, ending Qarmatian rule there.

abd-allah-ibn-ishaq.s: Abd Allah ibn Ishaq was a ruler of the Banu Ghaniya, the Almoravid family that held Majorca after the Almoravid collapse in Morocco and al-Andalus. While his brothers waged war against the Almohads in Ifriqiya, he governed the island until an Almohad fleet conquered Majorca in…

abd-allah-ibn-qasim.s: Abd Allah ibn Qasim was the founder of the Taifa of Alpuente in the Valencian uplands, ruling from the fortress town of Alpuente in the early 11th century after the collapse of the Caliphate of Córdoba. He took the honorific title Yumn al-Dawla.

abd-al-malik-ibn-hudhayl.s: Abd al-Malik ibn Hudhayl was ruler of the Taifa of Albarracín, a mountain principality of eastern al-Andalus, from about 1045 to 1103, a member of the Berber Banu Razin family. His long reign kept the small state alive between the taifas of Toledo, Zaragoza and Valencia,…

abd-al-malik-imad-al-dawla.s: Abd al-Malik Imad al-Dawla was the last Hudid ruler of the Taifa of Zaragoza. He succeeded his father al-Musta'in II in 1110 but lost the city to the Almoravids that same year.

abd-al-nabi-ibn-ali-ibn-mahdi.n: Abd al-Nabi ibn Ali ibn Mahdi
abd-al-nabi-ibn-ali-ibn-mahdi.s: Abd al-Nabi ibn Ali ibn Mahdi was the second ruler of the Mahdid dynasty of Yemen, succeeding his father, who had taken Zabid from the Najahids in 1159. He ran a militant state that, according to hostile sources, treated other Muslims as unbelievers, and he campaigned widely…

abd-al-rahman-al-ghafiqi.s: Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi was the Umayyad governor of al-Andalus in 721 and again from 730. In 732 he led a large raid across the Pyrenees into Gaul, sacked Bordeaux and advanced towards Tours, but was defeated and killed by the Frankish leader Charles Martel at the Battle of…

abd-rabbuh-mansur-hadi.s: Abd Rabbuh Mansur Hadi is a Yemeni politician who was vice-president under Ali Abdullah Saleh from 1994 and became president in 2012, after the 2011 uprising forced Saleh to hand over power. The Houthis seized Sanaa in 2014 and he fled to Aden and then Saudi Arabia, prompting…

abdal-khan.s: Abdal Khan was the Kurdish emir of Bitlis in the mid-17th century, ruling a hereditary principality under Ottoman overlordship. The traveller Evliya Çelebi described his rich court in 1655, shortly before an Ottoman army under Melek Ahmed Pasha attacked him for his defiance.

abdallah-ibn-tahir.s: Abdallah ibn Tahir was the most celebrated ruler of the Tahirid dynasty, governing Khurasan for the Abbasid Caliphate from 828 to 845 from his capital at Nishapur. Loyal but autonomous, he sent tribute to Baghdad while ruling the eastern provinces in his own right.

abdirashid-ali-shermarke.s: Abdirashid Ali Shermarke was a Somali politician, prime minister from 1960 to 1964 and president of the Somali Republic from 1967. His governments pursued the union of all Somali-inhabited lands, backing insurgents in Kenya's Northern Frontier District.

abdul-ghafur-khan.s: Abdul Ghafur Khan was the founder of Jaora State in Malwa, central India. A Pathan cavalry commander and brother-in-law of the freebooter Amir Khan, founder of Tonk, he received Jaora and nearby lands from the Holkar ruler of Indore, a grant confirmed by the British in 1818.

abdul-jalil-of-asahan.s: Abdul Jalil is the traditional founder of the Asahan Sultanate on the east coast of Sumatra, said to have been a son of Sultan Iskandar Muda of Aceh by a local woman. According to tradition he established the sultanate around 1630 at the mouth of the Asahan river, and his…

abdul-kahir.s: Abdul Kahir was the first sultan of Bima on the island of Sumbawa, in present-day Indonesia, ruling from around 1620 to 1640. He adopted Islam under the influence of the Gowa Sultanate of Makassar, and marriages with the Makassarese royal house bound the two courts closely…

abdul-karim-yakut-khan.s: Abdul Karim Yakut Khan was the first Nawab of Sachin, near Surat in Gujarat. A claimant to Janjira, the island fortress of the Siddi rulers on the Konkan coast, he renounced his rights there in 1791 under an arrangement made by the Peshwa's government and received the lands of…

abdul-qawi-mackawee.s: Abdul Qawi Mackawee was a nationalist politician in the British-ruled State of Aden. Appointed chief minister in 1965, he sided with the nationalists against the Federation of South Arabia and British policy and was dismissed later that year, after which Britain ruled Aden…

abdul-rauf-khan.s: Abdul Rauf Khan was the founder of Savanur State in northern Karnataka. An Afghan (Miana) officer in Mughal service, he received a grant in the Carnatic from the emperor Aurangzeb around 1680.

abdul-samad-khan-of-dujana.s: Abdul Samad Khan was the founder of Dujana State, a small Pathan principality in Haryana. A cavalry leader, he served Lord Lake in the Second Anglo-Maratha War, and in 1806 the British granted him Dujana and its villages as a reward.

abdullah-of-pahang.s: Abdullah of Pahang, Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin, became sultan of Pahang in January 2019 on the abdication of his father, Sultan Ahmad Shah. Later that month he was elected Yang di-Pertuan Agong, the king of Malaysia, and served a five-year term until January 2024, a period…

abdullah-of-baguirmi.s: Abdullah was mbang (king) of Baguirmi, south-east of Lake Chad, in the late 16th and early 17th centuries. Islam was adopted at the court of Massenya during his reign, and he expanded the kingdom through wars and slave raids against its neighbours, laying the foundations of…

abdullah-afeef.s: Abdullah Afeef was a Maldivian leader who became president of the breakaway United Suvadive Republic in 1959. A notable of Addu Atoll, where Britain had an air base at Gan, he led the southern atolls' revolt against the government in Malé over taxes and trade restrictions.

abdullah-i-of-jordan.s: Abdullah I of Jordan, a son of Sharif Hussein of Mecca, was a leader of the Arab Revolt and became emir of Transjordan under the British mandate in 1921. On 25 May 1946 he was proclaimed king of the independent kingdom, renamed Jordan in 1949.

abdullah-ibn-rashid.s: Abdullah ibn Rashid was the founder of the Rashidi dynasty of Jabal Shammar in northern Arabia. In 1836 he took control of Ha'il, the main town of the region, with the backing of the Saudi ruler Faisal ibn Turki, and governed as emir until his death.

abdullah-ii-of-jordan.s: Abdullah II of Jordan has been king since 1999, succeeding his father Hussein. Trained as a soldier, he has kept the Hashemite monarchy stable through regional wars and the Arab Spring, while Jordan has taken in large numbers of Iraqi and Syrian refugees.

abdullah-khan-ii.s: Abdullah Khan II was the most powerful ruler of the Shaybanid dynasty in Transoxiana, effectively in power from the 1550s and khan from 1583 to 1598. He reunited the Uzbek appanages under Bukhara, took Herat and Mashhad from the Safavids and built caravanserais, bridges and…

abdurrahman-melek.s: Abdurrahman Melek was prime minister of the Hatay State, the short-lived republic formed in 1938 from the Sanjak of Alexandretta under French and Turkish supervision. He governed alongside the head of state Tayfur Sökmen while the state adopted Turkish laws, currency and…

abdyl-frasheri.s: Abdyl Frashëri was an Albanian politician and a leader of the League of Prizren, formed in 1878 to resist the partition of Albanian-inhabited lands after the Russo-Turkish War. A former deputy in the Ottoman parliament, he pressed for Albanian autonomy within the Ottoman Empire.

abel-muzorewa.s: Abel Muzorewa was a Methodist bishop and Rhodesian politician who led the United African National Council. He signed the Internal Settlement of 1978 with Ian Smith, and after the April 1979 elections became prime minister of Zimbabwe Rhodesia.

abgar-viii.s: Abgar VIII, called the Great, was king of Osroene, ruling from Edessa from about 177 to 212 CE. A Roman ally, he presided over a flourishing Syriac culture, and the Christian philosopher Bardaisan was at his court.

abikarib-asad.s: Abikarib As'ad was a king of Himyar in south Arabia in the late 4th and early 5th centuries. Under him Himyar extended its authority into central Arabia through the Kingdom of Kinda, a reach recorded in his inscriptions.

abil-oghlu.s: Abil Oghlu was the Taranchi leader who became sultan of Ili in 1866, after the Taranchis turned on their Dungan allies in the revolt against Qing rule. Ruling a farming population in the Ili valley from Ghulja, he fought the Dungans and the rival state of Kashgaria.

abish-khatun.s: Abish Khatun was the last ruler of the Salghurid dynasty of Fars, in southern Iran, placed on the throne as a child in 1263 under Mongol supervision. She was married to Mengü-Temür, a son of the Ilkhan Hülegü, and coins were struck in her name.

abiy-ahmed.s: Abiy Ahmed is an Ethiopian politician who became prime minister in 2018 after years of protests. He made peace with Eritrea, ending the long stalemate after the border war, and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2019.

abraham-fischer.s: Abraham Fischer was a politician of the Orange Free State and its successor, the Orange River Colony. He served on the Free State executive and as one of its envoys to Europe during the Second Boer War.

abraham-van-peere.s: Abraham van Peere was a merchant of Vlissingen in Zeeland who founded the Dutch colony of Berbice in present-day Guyana. In 1627 he received a charter from the Dutch West India Company to settle the Berbice river, and his family held the colony as a private patroonship for…

abu-abdallah-muhammad-afrighid.s: Abu Abdallah Muhammad was the last Afrighid shah of Khwarazm, ruling from Kath on the lower Amu Darya in the late 10th century. In 995 the emir of the rival city of Gurganj, Ma'mun ibn Muhammad, overthrew and killed him and founded the Ma'munid dynasty, uniting Khwarazm under…

abu-al-baqa-khalid.s: Abu al-Baqa Khalid was a Hafsid prince who ruled the Hafsid emirate of Bejaia from 1301, succeeding his father Abu Zakariya. In 1309 he took Tunis and reunited the two Hafsid realms as sultan, but his rule there was brief: he was overthrown and killed in 1311.

abu-al-fath-dawud.s: Abu al-Fath Dawud was the Ismaili ruler of Multan in the early 11th century, of the dynasty that had held the city since the late 10th century. Allied with the Fatimids, he was attacked by Mahmud of Ghazni in 1006, and Mahmud annexed Multan around 1010, persecuting its…

abu-al-fida.s: Abu al-Fida was an Ayyubid prince, historian and geographer who ruled Hama under Mamluk overlordship from 1310 until his death in 1331. A friend of the Mamluk sultan al-Nasir Muhammad, he received the title of sultan.

abu-al-hazm-ibn-jahwar.s: Abu al-Hazm ibn Jahwar was a Córdoban vizier who became head of the Taifa of Córdoba in 1031, when the city's notables deposed Hisham III and abolished the Caliphate of Córdoba. He governed through a council of leading citizens, presenting himself as an administrator rather…

abu-al-khattab-al-maafiri.s: Abu al-Khattab al-Ma'afiri was an Arab Ibadi leader elected imam in 757 by the Ibadi Berbers of Tripolitania and the Jebel Nafusa. His forces took Tripoli and in 758 Kairouan, ending the rule of the Sufri Warfajuma there.

abu-al-makarim-hibat-allah.s: Abu al-Makarim Hibat Allah was the chief of an Arab tribal group of the Rabi'a settled on Egypt's southern frontier around Aswan. In 1006 the Fatimid caliph al-Hakim gave him the title Kanz al-Dawla for capturing the rebel Abu Rakwa, and his successors took their name, the…

abu-al-misk-kafur.s: Abu al-Misk Kafur was a eunuch of African origin, once a slave, who became ruler of Ikhshidid Egypt. After al-Ikhshid died in 946 he governed as regent for his two sons and from 966 in his own name, holding Egypt, Syria and the Hijaz.

abu-al-qasim-muhammad-ibn-abbad.s: Abu al-Qasim Muhammad ibn Abbad was the qadi of Seville who founded the Abbadid dynasty. In 1023 the city's leading families expelled the Hammudid garrison and entrusted Seville to him.

abu-al-qasim-samgu.s: Abu al-Qasim Samgu was a leader of the Miknasa Berbers and a Sufri Kharijite who became ruler of Sijilmasa after the deposition of its first leader, Isa ibn Yazid, in 772. He founded the line of the Banu Midrar, which gave the Midrarid Emirate its name and ruled the Saharan…

abu-bakr-ahmad-ibn-tahir.s: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Tahir was the head of the Banu Tahir, a local family who took effective control of the Taifa of Murcia in the 11th century. Murcia had been governed for the Amirid rulers of Almería and Valencia, but under him the family ruled as patricians, nominally under…

abu-bakr-ibn-sad.s: Abu Bakr ibn Sa'd was atabeg of Fars of the Salghurid dynasty from 1226 to 1260. By submitting to the Mongol Great Khan Ögedei and paying tribute, he saved Fars and Shiraz from destruction.

abu-dulaf.s: Abu Dulaf al-Qasim ibn Isa was an Arab general and poet of the Banu Ijl who served the Abbasid caliphs Harun al-Rashid and al-Ma'mun. Around 825 he founded the city of Karaj in the Jibal region of western Iran, which became the seat of his family, the Dulafids, who governed…

abu-hammu-musa-ii.s: Abu Hammu Musa II was sultan of the Zayyanid Kingdom of Tlemcen from 1359 to 1389. He restored the dynasty after a period of Marinid occupation and spent much of his reign fighting the Marinids and rebellious Arab tribes.

abu-hassun-al-semlali.s: Abu Hassun al-Semlali was a sharif and descendant of the saint Sidi Ahmed ou Moussa who built a principality in the Tazeroualt region of the Anti-Atlas in southern Morocco. As the Saadi Sultanate broke up in the early 17th century, he took control of the Sous and its Saharan…

abu-isa-ibn-labbun.s: Abu Isa ibn Labbun was a Valencian notable who made himself master of Murviedro, the ancient Saguntum, after al-Qadir was installed in Valencia as a Castilian client in 1086. Known only from brief chronicle notices, his small lordship was caught up in the struggles for the…

abu-ishaq-inju.s: Abu Ishaq Inju was the last Injuid ruler of Fars, governing from Shiraz from about 1343. A cultivated and lavish ruler, he was visited by Ibn Battuta and patronised the poets Hafez and Ubayd Zakani.

abu-ja.s: Abu Ja, also called Jatau, was a ruler of the Hausa dynasty of Zazzau driven into exile by the Fulani jihad. After his brother Muhammadu Makau fled south to Zuba and died there, Abu Ja succeeded him and around 1828 founded a new walled town that took his name, Abuja.

abu-muhammad-abd-al-wahid-ibn-abi-hafs.n: Abu Muhammad Abd al-Wahid ibn Abi Hafs
abu-muhammad-abd-al-wahid-ibn-abi-hafs.s: Abu Muhammad Abd al-Wahid ibn Abi Hafs was an Almohad governor of Ifriqiya and a son of Abu Hafs Umar, a companion of the Almohad founder Ibn Tumart. Appointed in 1207, he governed the province from Tunis with wide autonomy until his death in 1221.

abu-numayy-ii.s: Abu Numayy II was Sharif of Mecca, sharing rule with his father from 1512 and governing alone from 1525 until his death in 1584. He recognised Ottoman overlordship after the Ottoman conquest of Egypt in 1517 and extended the sharifate's authority over much of the Hijaz.

abu-nur-hilal-ibn-abi-qurra.n: Abu Nur Hilal ibn Abi Qurra
abu-nur-hilal-ibn-abi-qurra.s: Abu Nur Hilal ibn Abi Qurra was a chief of the Banu Ifran, a Zanata Berber clan, who made himself independent at Ronda around 1015, at first as a governor for the Hammudid caliphs. He founded the Taifa of Ronda, centred on the gorge-top town, which his family held until the…

abu-said-al-jannabi.s: Abu Sa'id al-Jannabi was an Ismaili missionary who founded the Qarmatian state of Bahrain in eastern Arabia. From 899, preaching the coming of the Mahdi, he won over Bedouin and peasants and took al-Ahsa and Qatif.

abu-taghlib.s: Abu Taghlib was the Hamdanid emir of Mosul who deposed his father Nasir al-Dawla in 967. He became entangled in the struggles of the Buyid dynasty, backing Izz al-Dawla against Adud al-Dawla.

abu-tahir-ibn-muhammad.s: Abu Tahir ibn Muhammad was the founder of the Hazaraspid dynasty of Luristan in south-western Iran. A Kurdish or Lur commander in the service of the Salghurid dynasty of Fars, he was sent around 1148 to subdue the region and made himself its ruler.

abu-uthman-said-ibn-hakam.s: Abu Uthman Said ibn Hakam was ra'is of Muslim Menorca from 1234 until his death in 1282, ruling from Madina Manurqa, the later Ciutadella, as a tributary of the Crown of Aragon. A scholar and poet, he gathered a library and kept the island prosperous through farming, livestock…

abu-yusuf-yaqub-ibn-abd-al-haqq.n: Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq
abu-yusuf-yaqub-ibn-abd-al-haqq.s: Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq was sultan of the Marinid dynasty of Morocco from 1258 to 1286. In 1269 he captured Marrakesh, ending Almohad rule, and in 1276 he founded the royal city of Fes el-Jdid beside Fez.

abu-zayd-almohad-governor-of-valencia.s: Abu Zayd was an Almohad prince, a descendant of the caliph Abd al-Mu'min, and the last Almohad governor of Valencia. In 1229 Zayyan ibn Mardanish overthrew him, and he fled to James I of Aragon, became his vassal and later converted to Christianity, aiding the Aragonese…

abubakar-tafawa-balewa.s: Abubakar Tafawa Balewa was a Nigerian politician of the Northern People's Congress who became federal prime minister in 1957 and led Nigeria to independence on 1 October 1960. He remained prime minister of the independent federation until he was killed in the military coup of…

abul-hasan-qutb-shah.s: Abul Hasan Qutb Shah, known as Tana Shah, was the last sultan of Golconda in the Deccan, reigning from 1672 to 1687. His Brahmin ministers Madanna and Akkanna ran the government.

abul-aswar-shavur-i.s: Abu'l-Aswar Shavur I was the Shaddadid emir of Ganja in the south Caucasus from 1049 to 1067, having earlier ruled Dvin. A forceful soldier and patron, he fought and allied in turn with the Armenians, Georgians and Byzantines, and accepted Seljuk overlordship.

abul-fadl-nasr-ibn-ahmad.s: Abu'l-Fadl Nasr ibn Ahmad was the founder of the Nasrid line of maliks of Sistan, a branch of the Saffarid dynasty. In 1029, after the Ghaznavid Empire had absorbed Sistan, he established himself at Zaranj.

abul-ghazi-bahadur.s: Abu'l-Ghazi Bahadur was khan of Khiva from about 1643 to 1663 and a noted historian. After years of exile in Safavid Iran he took the throne, fought the Kalmyks and Bukhara and strengthened the khanate.

abul-harith-muhammad.s: Abu'l-Harith Muhammad was the Farighunid amir of Guzgan, in present-day northern Afghanistan, in the late 10th century. A patron of learning, he was the dedicatee of the Hudud al-Alam, an anonymous Persian geography of the known world completed in 982.

abul-hayja-wahsudan.s: Abu'l-Hayja Wahsudan was the Rawwadid emir of Azerbaijan, ruling north-western Iran from Tabriz from about 1019 to 1059. He fought the Armenian kingdoms and the Georgians and welcomed the poet Qatran Tabrizi, whose verses record the destructive earthquake of 1042 at Tabriz.

abulkhair-khan.s: Abulkhair Khan was khan of the Junior Juz, the western Kazakh horde, from about 1718. Under pressure from the Dzungars and the Kalmyk Khanate he sought Russian protection, formalised in 1731, the first step in Russia's absorption of the Kazakh steppe.

abul-shawk-faris.s: Abu'l-Shawk Faris was the leading ruler of the Annazid dynasty, Kurdish lords of the Zagros passes between Iraq and Iran, from 1011 to 1046. He extended their power from Hulwan to Dinavar and Kermanshah, playing the Buyids, Kakuyids and other neighbours against each other.

aceh-war.s: The Aceh War was the long conflict between the Netherlands and the Aceh Sultanate in northern Sumatra, begun by a Dutch invasion in 1873. The Dutch took the capital but faced decades of guerrilla resistance led by Islamic scholars and chiefs.

achaean-war.s: The Achaean War of 146 BCE was the conflict in which Rome crushed the Achaean League and its allies in southern Greece. After the league defied Roman demands, the consul Lucius Mummius defeated its army near Corinth and sacked the city.

achirimbi-ii.s: Achirimbi II was Fon of Bafut, a kingdom in the Grassfields of north-western Cameroon, from 1932 to 1968. He ruled under British administration and into independent Cameroon.

act-of-mediation.s: The Act of Mediation was the constitution imposed on Switzerland by Napoleon Bonaparte in 1803, replacing the unstable Helvetic Republic after civil strife in 1802. It restored the cantons in a new confederation of nineteen, including newly created cantons such as Vaud, Aargau…

adalbert-ii-of-tuscany.s: Adalbert II, called the Rich, was margrave of Tuscany from 886 until his death in 915, ruling from Lucca. The son of Adalbert I, he made the margraves among the most powerful lords in Italy and played a leading part in the struggles for the Italian crown.

adam-of-bremen.s: Adam of Bremen was a German chronicler who wrote the Deeds of the Bishops of Hamburg, a history of the archbishopric of Hamburg-Bremen, around 1075. Its fourth book is the most important early description of Scandinavia and the Baltic, including the pagan temple at Uppsala and…

adelaide-del-vasto.s: Adelaide del Vasto was the third wife of Roger I, Count of Sicily, and regent of the County of Sicily for her young sons from 1101 to 1112. She moved the court to Palermo and prepared the way for her son Roger II, later the first King of Sicily.

adelaide-of-susa.s: Adelaide of Susa was the heiress of the March of Turin and one of the most powerful rulers in 11th-century Italy. Her marriage to Otto of Savoy brought the Arduinici lands in Piedmont to the house of Savoy.

adib-shishakli.s: Adib Shishakli was a Syrian army officer who took part in the coups of 1949 and ruled Syria as its military strongman from late 1949 to 1954, as president from 1953. His authoritarian rule provoked a revolt and a military rising that forced him into exile in 1954, after which…

adityawarman.s: Adityawarman was a Sumatran king of Malayu and Javanese descent who had served Majapahit before founding his own kingdom in the Minangkabau highlands. In 1347 he inscribed the back of the Amoghapasa statue of Dharmasraya, declaring himself king, and he later ruled from the…

adna-chaffee.s: Adna Chaffee was a United States Army officer who commanded the American contingent in the relief of the Beijing legations during the Boxer Rebellion in 1900. In 1901 he succeeded Arthur MacArthur as military governor of the Philippines, a post that ended in 1902 as civil…

adolf-ii-of-holstein.s: Adolf II of Holstein was count of Holstein and Stormarn from 1130, of the house of Schauenburg. He pushed German settlement into Slavic Wagria and in 1143 founded Lübeck, which later passed to Henry the Lion.

adolf-ii-prince-of-schaumburg-lippe.s: Adolf II was the last reigning prince of Schaumburg-Lippe, a small state of the German Empire, succeeding his father George in 1911. He abdicated in November 1918 during the German Revolution, and the state continued as the Free State of Schaumburg-Lippe.

adolf-of-cleves-lord-of-ravenstein.n: Adolf of Cleves, Lord of Ravenstein
adolf-of-cleves-lord-of-ravenstein.s: Adolf of Cleves, Lord of Ravenstein, was a younger son of Adolf I, Duke of Cleves, and a nephew of Philip the Good of Burgundy. He held the lordship of Ravenstein and was a leading figure at the Burgundian court, serving in its wars and government in the Low Countries.

adriaan-van-jaarsveld.s: Adriaan van Jaarsveld was a frontier farmer and commando leader on the eastern border of the Dutch Cape Colony, known for campaigns against the Xhosa. In February 1795 he and Marthinus Prinsloo led the burghers of Graaff-Reinet in expelling the landdrost Honoratus Maynier and…

adrian-von-bubenberg.s: Adrian von Bubenberg was a Bernese knight and statesman, several times Schultheiss (mayor) of Bern. In the Burgundian Wars he defended the town of Murten against the army of Charles the Bold in 1476, holding out until the Swiss confederates won the Battle of Murten.

aed-findliath.s: Áed Findliath was king of Ailech, of the northern Uí Néill, and High King of Ireland from 862 to 879. He fought the Vikings, destroying their camps along the northern coast in 866, and strengthened the power of the Cenél nEógain.

aed-slaine.s: Áed Sláine was a king of the southern Uí Néill in Ireland, from whom the Síl nÁedo Sláine descended. Remembered as joint High King of Ireland until his murder in 604, he gave his name to the kindred that established itself in the plain of Brega in the 7th century, ruling the…

aedan-mac-gabrain.s: Áedán mac Gabráin was king of Dál Riata, the Gaelic kingdom of Argyll and north-eastern Ireland, from about 574 to about 609. Said to have been inaugurated by Saint Columba, he campaigned widely against the Picts and Britons, but was defeated by Æthelfrith of Northumbria at…

aelle-of-sussex.s: Ælle of Sussex was the first recorded king of the South Saxons. The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle says that he and his three sons landed in 477, fought the Britons near the shore and in 491 stormed the Roman fort of Anderitum (Pevensey).

aelle-of-deira.s: Ælle of Deira was the first known king of Deira, the Anglian kingdom of east Yorkshire, ruling from about 560 according to the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle. Bede tells how Pope Gregory the Great, meeting Deiran slave boys in Rome, punned on the king's name, saying Alleluia should be…

aethelstan.s: Æthelstan was king of the Anglo-Saxons from 924 and the first king of all England from 927, when he took York and received the submission of northern rulers. A grandson of Alfred the Great, he defeated an alliance of Scots, Vikings and Strathclyde Britons at the Battle of…

aflah-ibn-abd-al-wahhab.s: Aflah ibn Abd al-Wahhab was the third imam of the Rustamid Imamate, the Ibadi state centred on Tahert in present-day Algeria, ruling for about fifty years in the 9th century. His long reign is remembered as the high point of the dynasty, when Tahert prospered from Saharan…

afonso-costa.s: Afonso Costa was a Portuguese lawyer and leader of the Democratic Party who dominated politics in the First Portuguese Republic. As justice minister he drafted the 1911 law separating church and state, and he served three times as prime minister between 1913 and 1917, taking…

afonso-i-of-portugal.s: Afonso I of Portugal, known as Afonso Henriques, was the first king of Portugal. Son of Count Henry of the County of Portugal, he took power in 1128, proclaimed himself king after the Battle of Ourique in 1139 and was recognised by León in 1143 and by the papacy in 1179.

afonso-iii-of-portugal.s: Afonso III of Portugal was king from 1248 to 1279. He completed the Portuguese reconquest by taking Faro and the rest of the Algarve in 1249, and the Treaty of Badajoz of 1267 settled the territory in Portugal's favour.

africa-nova.s: Africa Nova, 'New Africa', was the Roman province created by Julius Caesar in 46 BCE from the eastern part of the Kingdom of Numidia after his victory at Thapsus; the historian Sallust was its first governor. It was later merged with the older province of Africa Vetus to form…

african-lakes-company.s: The African Lakes Company was a Scottish trading company founded in Glasgow in 1878 to support the Presbyterian missions around Lake Malawi and to replace the slave trade with legitimate commerce. From its base at Karonga it fought Swahili-Arab slave traders in the Karonga War…

african-national-congress.s: The African National Congress is a South African political party founded in 1912 as the South African Native National Congress to defend the rights of Black South Africans. It led opposition to apartheid, was banned in 1960 and turned to armed struggle, and its leader Nelson…

afro-shirazi-party.s: The Afro-Shirazi Party was a Zanzibari political party formed in 1957 to represent the islands' African and Shirazi majority. Led by Abeid Karume, it came to power after the Zanzibar Revolution of January 1964 and ruled the People's Republic of Zanzibar as a single party.

agesilaus-ii.s: Agesilaus II was king of Sparta from about 400 to 360 BCE, during the period of Spartan supremacy after the Peloponnesian War. He campaigned against Persia in Asia Minor, won at Coronea in 394 BCE during the Corinthian War, and led Sparta through its decline after the defeat…

aghlabid-dynasty.s: The Aghlabid dynasty ruled Ifriqiya, roughly present-day Tunisia and eastern Algeria, from Kairouan as hereditary emirs under nominal Abbasid authority from 800 to 909. In 827 they began the long conquest of Byzantine Sicily, which created the Emirate of Sicily.

ah-kukum-xiu.s: Ah Kukum Xiu was the ruler of the Maya province of Maní in Yucatán, head of the Xiu lineage, in the mid-16th century. In 1542 he submitted to Francisco de Montejo the Younger at T'ho, the future Mérida, giving the Spanish an important native ally in their conquest of Yucatán.

ahilyabai-holkar.s: Ahilyabai Holkar was the Maratha queen who ruled the Holkar domains of Malwa, later Indore State, from 1767 until her death in 1795. Governing from Maheshwar on the Narmada, she was known for able administration and justice, and for building and restoring temples, wells and…

ahmad-bakhsh-khan.s: Ahmad Bakhsh Khan was the first Nawab of Loharu. An agent who helped the British in their dealings with the ruler of Alwar during the Second Anglo-Maratha War, he received Loharu from Alwar and Firozpur Jhirka from the British in 1806.

ahmad-i-bey.s: Ahmad I Bey was the Husainid bey of Tunis from 1837 to 1855. He modernised the army on European lines, founded a military school at Bardo and built factories, and abolished slavery in Tunisia in 1846, before France or the United States.

ahmad-bin-rashid-al-mualla.s: Ahmad bin Rashid Al Mualla was ruler of Umm al-Quwain, one of the Trucial States, from 1929 to 1981. His long rule spanned the period of British protection and the founding of the United Arab Emirates, which Umm al-Quwain joined in December 1971.

ahmad-ibn-said-al-busaidi.s: Ahmad ibn Said al-Busaidi was the founder of the Al Bu Said dynasty of Oman. As governor of Sohar in the 1740s he resisted the Persian forces drawn in by the Ya'aruba civil war, drove them out and was elected imam.

ahmad-ibn-tulun.s: Ahmad ibn Tulun was a Turkish soldier sent to govern Egypt for the Abbasids in 868 who made himself its independent ruler and founded the Tulunid dynasty. He built a strong army and navy, extended his rule into Syria, and founded a new capital, al-Qata'i, whose great Mosque of…

ahmad-ibn-yahya-al-yahsubi.s: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Yahsubi was the founder of the Taifa of Niebla in south-western al-Andalus. Of an Arab family long settled in the region, he made himself independent around 1023, when the Caliphate of Córdoba was breaking up into taifa kingdoms.

ahmad-khan-bangash.s: Ahmad Khan Bangash was the Afghan Nawab of Farrukhabad from 1750 to 1771. Soon after his accession he defeated an army of the Nawab of Awadh in 1750, but a combined Maratha and Awadh force crushed him in 1751.

ahmad-khan-donboli.s: Ahmad Khan Donboli was khan of Khoy from 1763 to 1786 and the most powerful ruler of the Kurdish Donboli family. From Khoy and Salmas he extended his influence over Tabriz and much of north-western Iran during the period of Zand supremacy.

ahmad-khan-muqaddam.s: Ahmad Khan Muqaddam was the best-known khan of Maragheh, a small khanate south-east of Lake Urmia ruled by the Muqaddam family in the 18th century. Like other local khans of Azerbaijan he kept his own troops, paid tribute to the dominant power of the day and contended with the…

ahmad-nami.s: Ahmad Nami was a Syrian politician of Circassian origin, a son-in-law of the Ottoman sultan Abdul Hamid II, who served as head of the French-mandated State of Syria from 1926 to 1928. Appointed by the French during the Great Syrian Revolt, he headed a government that failed to…

ahmad-sayf-al-nasr.s: Ahmad Sayf al-Nasr was the leader of the Awlad Sulayman's Sayf al-Nasr family, which had long resisted Italian rule in Fezzan. After Free French forces took Fezzan in 1943, he served as chief of the territory under French military administration.

ahmadou-ahidjo.s: Ahmadou Ahidjo was a Cameroonian politician from the Muslim north who became prime minister of French Cameroon in 1958 and led it to independence in 1960. As first president of Cameroon he united it with the former British Southern Cameroons in 1961, created a one-party state…

ahmadu-tall.s: Ahmadu Tall was the son and successor of El Hadj Umar Tall and ruler of the Toucouleur Empire from Ségou after his father's death in 1864. He struggled with rival brothers and rebellious subjects while negotiating with the advancing French, who took Ségou in 1890 under Louis…
