ahmed-abdallah.s: Ahmed Abdallah was a Comorian politician who headed the government of the French Territory of the Comoros and unilaterally declared its independence on 6 July 1975. Overthrown within weeks, he returned to power with mercenary help in 1978 and ruled as president until he was…

ahmed-al-sharaa.s: Ahmed al-Sharaa, earlier known as Abu Mohammad al-Julani, is a Syrian militant leader and politician. As head of Hayat Tahrir al-Sham in Idlib he led the offensive that overthrew Bashar al-Assad in December 2024, ending more than five decades of Assad family rule, and he was…

ahmed-belkadi.s: Ahmed Belkadi was a Kabyle leader from a family of judges who founded the Kingdom of Kuku in the Djurdjura mountains around 1515. Allying at first with the Barbarossa brothers and then turning against them, he defeated Hayreddin Barbarossa in 1520 and held Algiers for several…

ahmed-muhtar-pasha.s: Ahmed Muhtar Pasha was an Ottoman general and statesman. In 1872 he led the expedition that took Sanaa and established the Yemen Vilayet, and he became a hero for his defence of eastern Anatolia in the Russo-Turkish War of 1877 to 1878, earning the title Gazi.

ajatashatru-of-kashi.s: Ajatashatru of Kashi was a king of Kashi, around Varanasi, named in the Brihadaranyaka and Kaushitaki Upanishads of the Later Vedic period. In these texts he instructs the Brahmin Gargya on the nature of the self, an example of a learned king teaching priests.

ajay-pal.s: Ajay Pal was a raja of the Panwar dynasty who in the 14th or 15th century subdued the many local chiefs of the central Himalaya and united the Garhwal Kingdom, named after their forts (garh). He moved his capital from Chandpur to Devalgarh and then to Srinagar on the…

aji-batara-agung-dewa-sakti.s: Aji Batara Agung Dewa Sakti is the founder of the Kutai Kartanegara kingdom in eastern Borneo according to the Salasilah Kutai chronicle. Around 1300 he is said to have established it at Kutai Lama near the mouth of the Mahakam River as a Hindu state oriented towards Majapahit.

aji-pangeran-sinum-panji-mendapa.s: Aji Pangeran Sinum Panji Mendapa was a ruler of Kutai Kartanegara in eastern Borneo in the early 17th century. In 1635 he conquered the ancient upriver Kingdom of Kutai Martadipura, uniting the Mahakam basin under one state, which became known as Kutai Kartanegara ing…

ajib-al-kafuta.s: Ajib al-Kafuta was the most famous chief of the Abdallab, the Arab rulers of northern Sudan who governed as viceroys of the Funj Sultanate. He sought greater independence from the Funj, extending his influence over the Nile and the pilgrimage routes, but was defeated and…

ajit-singh-of-ladwa.s: Ajit Singh was the raja of Ladwa, one of the Cis-Sutlej Sikh states under British protection after 1809. Despite this, he kept ties with the Sikh kingdom of Lahore and joined its side in the First Anglo-Sikh War of 1845 to 1846.

ajwad-ibn-zamil.s: Ajwad ibn Zamil was the greatest ruler of the Jabrid dynasty of eastern Arabia in the late 15th century. From al-Ahsa he controlled Qatif and the Bahrain islands, extended his influence towards Oman and made a celebrated pilgrimage to Mecca with a large retinue.

akechi-mitsuhide.s: Akechi Mitsuhide was a Japanese general in the service of Oda Nobunaga. In June 1582 he turned on his lord and attacked him at the Honnō-ji temple in Kyoto, where Nobunaga died.

al-bu-said-dynasty.s: The Al Bu Said dynasty has ruled Oman since the 1740s, when Ahmad ibn Said expelled the Persians and was elected imam in place of the Ya'aruba. Its sultans built a maritime empire from Muscat and Zanzibar over the Swahili coast; after 1856 the family split into separate Omani…

al-madhkur.s: The Al Madhkur were an Arab family settled on the Persian coast who ruled the port of Bushehr as sheikhs from the mid-18th century under Persian overlordship. They also governed Bahrain on behalf of Persia until 1783, when the Al Khalifa of Zubarah drove out their governor and…

al-sabah.s: Al Sabah is the ruling family of Kuwait, descended from the Bani Utbah clan that settled there in the early 18th century. Sabah I became the first sheikh around 1752.

ala-al-dawla-bozkurt.s: Ala al-Dawla Bozkurt was bey of the Dulkadirids, the Turkmen principality around Elbistan and Maraş, from 1480 to 1515. He balanced between the Ottomans and the Mamluks and fought the Safavids, but after Selim I's victory at Chaldiran he was defeated and killed by the Ottomans…

ala-al-dawla-muhammad.s: Ala al-Dawla Muhammad, known as Ibn Kakuya, was the founder of the Kakuyid dynasty. Appointed governor of Isfahan by the Buyids around 1008, he made himself independent ruler of Isfahan and Hamadan.

ala-al-din-husayn.s: Ala al-Din Husayn was ruler of Ghor from about 1149 to 1161. To avenge his brothers, killed by the Ghaznavid sultan, he sacked and burned Ghazni in 1150, earning the name Jahan-suz, 'World Burner'.

ala-singh.s: Ala Singh was a Sikh chief of the Phulkian family and the founder of Patiala State. From the 1720s he built up power in the Malwa region of Punjab and founded the fort of Patiala in 1763.

alaeddin-bey.s: Alaeddin Bey was ruler of the Karamanids in central Anatolia from about 1361. Though married to a daughter of the Ottoman sultan Murad I, he repeatedly fought the Ottomans, who defeated him in 1386 and again at Akçay in 1397, after which Bayezid I had him executed.

alan-i-king-of-brittany.s: Alan I, called the Great, was count of Vannes and from about 890 king of Brittany. He led the Bretons to a victory over the Vikings at Questembert in 888 and reunited the country after a period of division.

alan-ii-duke-of-brittany.s: Alan II, called Barbetorte or Twisted Beard, was a grandson of Alan the Great who grew up in exile in England. He returned in 936, drove the Vikings out of Nantes and Brittany by 939 and ruled as duke rather than king.

alaric-ii.s: Alaric II was king of the Visigoths from 484 to 507, ruling much of Gaul and Hispania from Toulouse. In 486 he handed over the fugitive Roman ruler Syagrius to Clovis, and in 506 he issued the Breviary of Alaric, a digest of Roman law for his Roman subjects.

ala-ud-din-bahman-shah.s: Ala-ud-Din Bahman Shah, born Hasan, was the founder of the Bahmani Sultanate in the Deccan. A commander in the Delhi Sultanate's southern provinces, he joined a revolt against Muhammad bin Tughluq and was proclaimed sultan in 1347, with his capital at Gulbarga.

alauddin-husain-shah.s: Alauddin Husain Shah was sultan of Bengal from 1494 to 1519 and founder of the Husain Shahi dynasty. He restored order after a period of palace coups, conquered Kamatapur around 1498, campaigned in Assam and Odisha, and patronised Bengali literature.

alauddin-riayat-shah-ii.s: Alauddin Riayat Shah II was the first sultan of Johor, a son of the last sultan of Malacca, Mahmud Shah. After the Portuguese took Malacca in 1511, he founded the Johor Sultanate on the Johor River around 1528 and continued the struggle against Portugal.

albemarle-sound.s: Albemarle Sound is a large estuary on the coast of North Carolina, sheltered from the Atlantic by the Outer Banks. Settlers from Virginia moved to its shores in the 1650s and 1660s, and the Albemarle region became the first settled part of the Province of Carolina and the core…

albert-i-of-belgium.s: Albert I was king of the Belgians from 1909 to 1934. He came to the throne a year after Belgium annexed the Congo Free State as the Belgian Congo, which he visited as heir in 1909, and supported reform of its administration.

albert-i-duke-of-bavaria.s: Albert I was a Wittelsbach duke of Bavaria-Straubing and count of Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland. He governed these lands from 1358 as regent for his insane brother William I and in his own right from 1389.

albert-ii-duke-of-brunswick-luneburg.s: Albert II, called the Fat, was a Guelph duke of Brunswick-Lüneburg who received the southern lands around Göttingen, Münden and Uslar in the partition of around 1291 and founded the Principality of Göttingen. He later also took over Wolfenbüttel, and his descendants founded…

albert-iii-duke-of-bavaria.s: Albert III was duke of Bavaria-Munich from 1438 to 1460. He is remembered for his secret marriage to Agnes Bernauer, a commoner whom his father Duke Ernest had drowned at Straubing in 1435.

albert-schweitzer.s: Albert Schweitzer was an Alsatian theologian, organist and physician, born at Kaysersberg in 1875. In 1913 he founded a hospital at Lambaréné in Gabon, then a French colony, where he worked for most of the rest of his life.

alberto-fujimori.s: Alberto Fujimori was president of Peru from 1990 to 2000. He curbed hyperinflation, closed Congress in a self-coup in 1992 and fought the Shining Path insurgency, whose leader was captured that year.

alberto-iii-pio.s: Alberto III Pio was the last Pio lord of Carpi, a humanist pupil of Aldus Manutius who rebuilt the town as a Renaissance showpiece with a new cathedral and square. A diplomat for France and the papacy, he was deprived of Carpi by Charles V in the 1520s, after which it passed…

alberto-scotti.s: Alberto Scotti was a Guelph nobleman and merchant who made himself lord of Piacenza in 1290. He was driven out and returned several times amid struggles with the Visconti and other Lombard lords, and his career illustrates the passage of Italian communes into signorie ruled by…

albertus-magnus.s: Albertus Magnus was a German Dominican friar, philosopher and scientist, teacher of Thomas Aquinas, who did much to bring Aristotle's works into Christian learning. He served briefly as bishop of Regensburg from 1260 to 1262 before resigning to return to teaching.

alboury-ndiaye.s: Alboury Ndiaye was the last independent buurba, or king, of Jolof in Senegal, ruling from 1875. He resisted French expansion, allying for a time with Lat Dior of Cayor, until a French column occupied Jolof in 1890.

alcide-de-gasperi.s: Alcide De Gasperi was an Italian statesman, founder of the Christian Democracy party, and prime minister from 1945 to 1953. He led Italy through the transition from monarchy to republic in 1946, anchored it in NATO and the Marshall Plan, and was one of the founders of European…

aldfrith-of-northumbria.s: Aldfrith was king of Northumbria from 685 to 705, succeeding his half-brother Ecgfrith after the defeat at Nechtansmere. Educated among the Irish, he was known as a scholar king.

aldfrith-of-lindsey.s: Aldfrith of Lindsey is the last king of Lindsey known from the surviving Anglian royal genealogies and from his witness to a charter of Offa of Mercia in the late 8th century. By then Lindsey, the small kingdom around Lincoln, was under Mercian overlordship, and no later…

alejandro-oreilly.s: Alejandro O'Reilly was an Irish-born general in Spanish service. In 1769 he arrived in New Orleans with troops, put down the creole Rebellion of 1768 against Spanish rule, executed its leaders and established Spanish law and administration in Louisiana before leaving in 1770.

aleko-bogoridi.s: Aleko Bogoridi was an Ottoman Bulgarian statesman and diplomat. Under the Treaty of Berlin he was appointed the first governor-general of Eastern Rumelia, the autonomous Ottoman province south of the Balkan Mountains, serving from 1879 to 1884.

aleksandras-stulginskis.s: Aleksandras Stulginskis was a Lithuanian Christian Democrat politician who chaired the Constituent Assembly from 1920 and served as president of Lithuania from 1920 to 1926, overseeing land reform and the 1922 constitution. After the Soviet occupation he was deported to a…

aleuas-the-red.s: Aleuas the Red was a semi-legendary ruler of Larissa in the 6th century BCE, ancestor of the Aleuadae, the leading aristocratic family of Thessaly. He was credited with dividing Thessaly into four districts, the tetrads, and with fixing the cavalry and hoplites each district…

alexander-baranov.s: Alexander Baranov was a Russian merchant who managed the Russian fur-trading posts in Alaska from 1790 and became the first chief manager of the Russian-American Company in 1799. He founded New Archangel, present-day Sitka, which became the capital of Russian America after it…

alexander-jannaeus.s: Alexander Jannaeus was king and high priest of the Hasmonean kingdom of Judaea from 103 to 76 BCE. Through constant wars he extended the kingdom to its greatest size, taking coastal cities and lands east of the Jordan.

alexander-kerensky.s: Alexander Kerensky was a Russian socialist lawyer who served in the Provisional Government after the February Revolution of 1917, first as justice and war minister and from July as its head. He proclaimed Russia a republic in September 1917 and was overthrown by the Bolsheviks…

alexander-khatisian.s: Alexander Khatisian was an Armenian politician of the Dashnak party, formerly mayor of Tiflis. He served as prime minister of the First Republic of Armenia from 1919 to 1920 and signed the Treaty of Alexandropol with Turkey in December 1920, shortly before the Soviet takeover.

alexander-mcgillivray.s: Alexander McGillivray was a leader of the Muscogee (Creek) people, the son of a Scottish trader and a Creek mother. After the American Revolution he used alliances with Spain to resist encroachment by Georgia, and in 1790 he negotiated the Treaty of New York with the United…

alexander-obrenovic.s: Alexander Obrenović was king of Serbia from 1889 to 1903. His authoritarian rule, suspension of the constitution and unpopular marriage to Draga Mašin alienated the army.

alexander-of-battenberg.s: Alexander of Battenberg was a German prince elected the first ruler of the autonomous Principality of Bulgaria in 1879. He accepted the union with Eastern Rumelia in 1885 and defeated Serbia at Slivnitsa that year, but his independence angered Russia; pro-Russian officers…

alexander-of-pherae.s: Alexander of Pherae was tyrant of Pherae in Thessaly from 369 to 358 BCE. He sought to dominate Thessaly, imprisoned the Theban general Pelopidas and fought the Thebans, who defeated him at Cynoscephalae in 364 BCE and confined him to Pherae.

alexander-the-good.s: Alexander the Good was prince of Moldavia from 1400 to 1432. His long, mostly peaceful reign consolidated the young principality: he organised its administration, obtained a metropolitan see recognised by Constantinople, promoted trade through Suceava and Cetatea Albă, and…

alexandre-petion.s: Alexandre Pétion was a Haitian revolutionary leader and the first president of the Republic of Haiti in the south and west, from 1807 to 1818. Unlike Henri Christophe's northern kingdom, his republic distributed state lands to soldiers and peasants.

alexandros-svolos.s: Alexandros Svolos was a Greek professor of constitutional law who became president of the Political Committee of National Liberation (PEEA), the government set up by the EAM resistance in occupied Greece, in April 1944. He then joined the government of national unity of…

alexios-i-of-trebizond.s: Alexios I was the founder of the Empire of Trebizond. A grandson of the emperor Andronikos I Komnenos, he seized Trebizond in 1204 with his brother David and Georgian troops supplied by Queen Tamar, just as the Fourth Crusade took Constantinople.

alexios-of-theodoro.s: Alexios was prince of Theodoro, the Greek Orthodox principality of the Crimean mountains, in the early 15th century. He fought the Genoese of Caffa for access to the coast, built a port at Kalamita and strengthened the principality's ties with Trebizond through marriage.

alfonso-de-molina.s: Alfonso de Molina was a son of Alfonso IX of León and brother of Ferdinand III of Castile. Through his marriage to the heiress Mafalda he became lord of Molina, tying the semi-independent lordship to the Castilian royal family.

alfonso-fadrique.s: Alfonso Fadrique was an illegitimate son of King Frederick III of Sicily who governed the Catalan Duchy of Athens as vicar-general from 1317 to 1330. He took Neopatras and much of southern Thessaly from the Greeks and organised it as the Duchy of Neopatras in 1319,…

alfonso-ix-of-leon.s: Alfonso IX was king of León from 1188 to 1230. In his first year he summoned the Cortes of León, which included townsmen alongside nobles and clergy and is often cited as the earliest European parliament of its kind.

alfonso-x-of-castile.s: Alfonso X, called the Wise, was king of Castile and León from 1252 to 1284. He suppressed the Mudéjar revolt of 1264 to 1266 and brought the Kingdom of Murcia under direct Castilian rule.

alfred-dent.s: Alfred Dent was a British merchant who, with Baron von Overbeck, obtained concessions in northern Borneo from the sultans of Brunei and Sulu in 1877 and 1878. He founded the British North Borneo Company, which received a royal charter in 1881 and governed North Borneo until 1946.

alfred-freyberg.s: Alfred Freyberg was a German Nazi lawyer who in 1932 became minister-president of the Free State of Anhalt, the first Nazi to head a German state government. His government forced the Bauhaus out of Dessau that year.

alfred-milner.s: Alfred Milner was a British colonial administrator who as high commissioner for southern Africa from 1897 pressed the Transvaal into the Second Boer War. After the war he governed the Transvaal and Orange River Colonies until 1905, rebuilding their administration and gold…

alfred-sharpe.s: Alfred Sharpe was a British lawyer, hunter and colonial administrator who became commissioner of the British Central Africa Protectorate in 1896 and its first governor when it was renamed Nyasaland in 1907, serving until 1910. He extended British control over the territory…

alfredo-stroessner.s: Alfredo Stroessner was a Paraguayan general who seized power in 1954 and ruled as president until 1989, one of the longest dictatorships in Latin America. Backed by the Colorado Party and the army, his regime persecuted opponents and built the Itaipu dam with Brazil.

algirdas.s: Algirdas was grand duke of Lithuania from 1345 to 1377. Through his marriage to the heiress of Vitebsk he ruled that principality from about 1320, and as grand duke he expanded Lithuanian rule over much of present-day Belarus and Ukraine, defeating the Tatars at Blue Waters in…

algirdas-brazauskas.s: Algirdas Brazauskas was a Lithuanian politician who became first secretary of the Communist Party of Lithuania in 1988 and in 1989 led it to break away from the Soviet party, backing the independence movement. After independence he served as president from 1993 to 1998 and as…

al-harith-ibn-jabala.s: al-Harith ibn Jabala was king of the Ghassanids, the Christian Arab allies of the Byzantine Empire, from about 528 to 569. Justinian made him supreme phylarch over all Rome's Arab allies to counter the Lakhmids, and he killed the Lakhmid king al-Mundhir III in 554.

ali-abu-hassun.s: Ali Abu Hassun was the last Wattasid ruler of Morocco. After the Saadians took Fez in 1549, he obtained Ottoman support from Algiers and briefly retook the city in 1554, but was defeated and killed by the Saadian sultan Muhammad al-Shaykh later that year, ending the dynasty.

ali-al-mandri.s: Ali al-Mandri was a military leader from the Emirate of Granada who refounded Tetouan in northern Morocco around 1484, with Wattasid permission, rebuilding the ruined town with Andalusi refugees as a base against the Portuguese at Ceuta. His family ruled it for decades, and…

ali-aref-bourhan.s: Ali Aref Bourhan was an Afar politician who headed the government council of the French Territory of the Afars and the Issas, present-day Djibouti, from 1967 to 1976. He favoured continued ties with France, and his fall preceded the territory's independence as the Republic of…

ali-barid-shah-i.s: Ali Barid Shah I was ruler of the Bidar Sultanate in the Deccan from 1542 to 1580 and the first of the Barid dynasty to take the royal title. He joined the alliance of Deccan sultanates that defeated the Vijayanagara Empire at Talikota in 1565, and he patronised poetry and…

ali-ibn-hatim.s: Ali ibn Hatim was the last ruler of the Hamdanid sultanate of Sanaa, an Isma'ili tribal dynasty of 12th-century Yemen. When the Ayyubid prince Turan-Shah invaded Yemen in 1174, he fled to the mountains, and by the 1180s Sanaa had passed to Ayyubid rule, ending Isma'ili…

ali-ibn-mazyad.s: Ali ibn Mazyad was the founder of the Mazyadid dynasty, leaders of the Banu Asad Bedouin who controlled the Euphrates lands south of Baghdad. Recognised as a local ruler by the Buyids in the late 10th century, he established a Twelver Shia principality that his descendants…

ali-ibn-munqidh.s: Ali ibn Munqidh was the founder of the Munqidhite emirate of Shaizar on the Orontes in Syria. In 1081 he acquired the fortress of Shaizar from its bishop, who held it for Byzantium, and made it the seat of his family.

ali-ibn-rashid.s: Ali ibn Rashid was a sharif of the Banu Rashid who founded Chefchaouen in the Rif mountains of Morocco in 1471. He built it as a fortified base for holy war against the Portuguese enclaves around Ceuta and Ksar es-Seghir, and it became a refuge for Muslims and Jews from Granada.

ali-khamenei.s: Ali Khamenei is an Iranian cleric who served as president of Iran from 1981 to 1989 and then succeeded Ruhollah Khomeini as Supreme Leader in 1989. As the highest authority of the Islamic Republic he controlled the armed forces, the judiciary and state media, and shaped Iran's…

ali-shandora.s: Ali Shandora was emir of Trarza, a Moorish emirate north of the Senegal River in present-day Mauritania, in the early 18th century. He made Trarza a regional power, sought alliances with Morocco and traded gum arabic with the French and Dutch, and the emirs of Trarza came to…

ali-sher-khan-anchan.s: Ali Sher Khan Anchan was the most famous ruler of the Maqpon dynasty of Baltistan, reigning in the late 16th and early 17th centuries. From Skardu he campaigned into Ladakh, Gilgit and Chitral and is credited with building the Skardu fort and irrigation works.

ali-yaji.s: Ali Yaji was ruler of the Hausa kingdom of Kano in the 14th century. According to the Kano Chronicle, Islam was adopted at the court during his reign, brought by Wangara traders and scholars from Mali, and he was the first ruler to bear the title of sarki in the chronicle's…

alikhan-bukeikhanov.s: Alikhan Bukeikhanov was a Kazakh scholar and politician, a descendant of Genghis Khan through the Kazakh khans, and a member of the Russian Kadet party. In 1917 he became chairman of the Alash Orda, the government of the Alash Autonomy, which sought Kazakh self-rule during the…

alivardi-khan.s: Alivardi Khan was Nawab of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa from 1740 to 1756, having seized power by defeating Sarfaraz Khan at Giria. Much of his reign was spent fighting Maratha raids, ended by a treaty of 1751 that ceded Orissa's revenues.

ali-yi-muayyad.s: Ali-yi Mu'ayyad was the last leader of the Sarbadars, the Shia regime centred on Sabzevar in western Khorasan. He ruled from the 1360s and allied with Shia dervishes, but in 1381 submitted to Timur, in whose service he died in 1386, after which the Sarbadar lands passed into…

al-kamil-muhammad-of-mayyafariqin.s: al-Kamil Muhammad was the last Ayyubid ruler of Mayyafariqin in the Jazira, son of al-Muzaffar Ghazi. He refused to submit to the Mongols, who besieged Mayyafariqin from 1258 until it fell in 1260.

al-mansur-muhammad-ii-of-hama.s: al-Mansur Muhammad II was the Ayyubid prince of Hama from 1244 to 1284. When the Mongols invaded Syria in 1260 he joined the Mamluks and fought at Ain Jalut, and as a loyal Mamluk vassal he kept his principality when the other Ayyubid states disappeared.

al-muazzam-isa.s: al-Mu'azzam Isa was the Ayyubid ruler of Damascus from 1218 to 1227, a son of al-Adil and nephew of Saladin. During the Fifth Crusade he had the walls of Jerusalem dismantled in 1219 so that the Crusaders could not hold it.

almos.s: Álmos was a leader of the Hungarian tribal federation in the 9th century and the father of Árpád, founder of the Árpád dynasty. According to Hungarian tradition he was elected head of the seven tribes in Etelköz and led them until shortly before the conquest of the Carpathian…

almos-duke-of-croatia.s: Álmos was a Hungarian prince, the son of King Géza I, who held the ducal third of the kingdom, the tercia pars regni, and was briefly king of Croatia. His repeated plots against his brother King Coloman led Coloman to abolish the duchy in 1107 and later to have Álmos and his…

al-mundhir-ibn-al-harith.s: al-Mundhir ibn al-Harith was king of the Ghassanids from 569, succeeding his father al-Harith ibn Jabala as the Byzantine Empire's chief Arab ally. He defeated the Lakhmids and sacked their capital al-Hira, but was suspected of treachery by the emperors, arrested in 581 and…

alois-von-reding.s: Alois von Reding was a Swiss soldier and politician from Schwyz. In 1798 he led the forces of the central Swiss cantons against the French invasion and won brief successes before capitulating.

alonso-de-peralta.s: Alonso de Peralta was the last Spanish governor of Bougie, present-day Bejaia, in Algeria. In 1555 Salah Rais, beylerbey of Algiers, besieged the fortress, and Peralta surrendered it in return for his garrison's lives.

alp-arslan-al-akhras.s: Alp Arslan al-Akhras, 'the Mute', was the Seljuk ruler of Aleppo for about a year after his father Ridwan's death in 1113. A puppet of the eunuch Lu'lu', he had many of his father's officials and the city's Assassins killed, and was murdered by Lu'lu' in 1114.

alphonse-de-lamartine.s: Alphonse de Lamartine was a French Romantic poet and politician. In February 1848 he proclaimed the Second Republic from the Hôtel de Ville and led its provisional government as foreign minister, helping abolish slavery in the colonies.

al-qasim-ibn-muhammad-of-algeciras.s: al-Qasim ibn Muhammad was the last Hammudid ruler of the Taifa of Algeciras in southern al-Andalus, succeeding his father Muhammad ibn al-Qasim around 1048. Around 1058 the ruler of Seville, al-Mu'tadid, besieged the city and forced him to surrender it, and he retired to Córdoba.

as-salih-ayyub.s: As-Salih Ayyub was an Ayyubid prince who ruled Hisn Kayfa and the Jazira before becoming sultan of Egypt in 1240. He held Damascus in 1239 and again from 1245, retook Jerusalem with Khwarazmian help in 1244 and built up the Bahri Mamluk regiment.

az-zahir-ghazi.s: Az-Zahir Ghazi was a son of Saladin and Ayyubid ruler of Aleppo from 1186 to 1216. He kept his principality independent of his uncle al-Adil, strengthened Aleppo's citadel and built mosques and madrasas, making the city a centre of learning.

amadeus-vii-count-of-savoy.s: Amadeus VII, called the Red Count, was count of Savoy from 1383 to 1391. In 1388 Nice and its hinterland placed themselves under his protection in the act known as the Dedition, giving Savoy an outlet to the Mediterranean that it kept until 1860.

amadeus-viii-duke-of-savoy.s: Amadeus VIII was count of Savoy from 1391 and was raised to duke by Emperor Sigismund in 1416. In 1418 he inherited Piedmont, uniting it with Savoy, and he issued a law code for his lands.

amadu-seku.s: Amadu Seku was the son of Seku Amadu and the second ruler of the Massina Empire, the Fulbe Islamic state of the inner Niger delta, from 1845 to 1853. He kept up his father's religious and administrative order based at Hamdullahi.

amago-tsunehisa.s: Amago Tsunehisa was a Japanese warlord of the Sengoku period who rose from deputy governor to become master of Izumo, seizing Gassan-Toda castle in 1486. He expanded Amago power across the San'in region of western Honshu and contested the region with the Ōuchi, making the…

amago-yoshihisa.s: Amago Yoshihisa was the last head of the Amago clan of Izumo. After a long siege of Gassan-Toda castle by Mōri Motonari, he surrendered in 1566, ending the Amago as a ruling house.

amalric-i-of-jerusalem.s: Amalric I was king of Jerusalem from 1163 to 1174. Before his accession he held the County of Jaffa and Ascalon.

aman-andom.s: Aman Andom was an Ethiopian general of Eritrean origin who became the first chairman of the Derg, the military committee that deposed Emperor Haile Selassie, in September 1974. He opposed a military solution in Eritrea and the execution of former officials, and was killed…

amar-singh-i.s: Amar Singh I was Maharana of Mewar from 1597 to 1620, the son of Maharana Pratap. After years of war against Mughal armies, he made peace with Jahangir in 1615 on honourable terms: Mewar accepted Mughal overlordship, but the maharana was excused personal attendance at the…

amar-singh-of-patiala.s: Amar Singh was raja of Patiala from 1765 to 1782, grandson and successor of its founder Ala Singh. He received the title Raja-i-Rajgan from Ahmad Shah Durrani and enlarged the state through campaigns in the Punjab, making Patiala the leading Phulkian Sikh state.

amasis-ii.s: Amasis II was pharaoh of Egypt from 570 to 526 BCE, of the Twenty-sixth Dynasty. A general who took the throne after an army revolt against Apries, he ruled prosperously, allied with Greek states and gave Greek merchants the trading town of Naucratis.

ambracian-gulf.s: The Ambracian Gulf, now the Gulf of Arta, is an inlet of the Ionian Sea in north-western Greece. In antiquity it was bordered by Ambracia to the north and Acarnania to the south, and its narrow mouth at Actium saw Octavian's victory over Antony and Cleopatra in 31 BCE.

ambrosius-ehinger.s: Ambrosius Ehinger was a German agent of the Welser banking house of Augsburg and the first governor of their colony of Klein-Venedig in Venezuela from 1529. He founded Maracaibo in 1529 and led brutal expeditions inland in search of gold, on one of which he was killed by…

ame-pal.s: Ame Pal was a Tibetan warrior who around 1380 unified the upper Kali Gandaki valley and founded the kingdom of Lo, now Mustang in northern Nepal. He is credited with founding the walled capital Lo Manthang, and his descendants ruled Lo until the monarchy was abolished in 2008.

amenemhat-iii.s: Amenemhat III was a pharaoh of the Twelfth Dynasty who reigned for about 45 years in the 19th century BCE, the height of the Middle Kingdom. He developed the Faiyum with irrigation works, exploited the Sinai turquoise mines and built pyramids at Dahshur and Hawara, where his…

ameyaw-kwaakye.s: Ameyaw Kwaakye is a king of the Akan state of Bono, in the forest-savanna borderland of present-day Ghana, remembered in oral tradition. Tradition associates his reign with an expansion of gold mining, the source of Bono's wealth and of its trade with the north.

amir-barid-i.s: Amir Barid I was the son of Qasim Barid and the second ruler of the Barid dynasty of Bidar in the Deccan. Like his father he controlled the last Bahmani sultans as chief minister, and after the last of them fled around 1527 he ruled Bidar in his own right.

amira-dubbaj.s: Amira Dubbaj, also called Muzaffar Sultan, was the Ishaqid ruler of western Gilan, on the Caspian coast of Iran, in the early 16th century. He married a daughter of the Safavid shah Ismail I, linking the silk-rich province to the new dynasty.

an-qingxu.s: An Qingxu was the son of the rebel general An Lushan and the second emperor of the short-lived Yan state that rose against the Tang dynasty. He had his father murdered in 757 and took the throne, but lost Luoyang soon after to Tang and Uyghur forces.

anak-agung-anglurah-ketut-karangasem.s: Anak Agung Anglurah Ketut Karangasem was the last raja of Karangasem in eastern Bali. After the Dutch conquest of Lombok in 1894 Karangasem came under colonial control, and he governed it as a regent under Dutch supervision in the early 20th century.

anand-rao-puar.s: Anand Rao Puar was a Maratha commander who took part in the conquest of Malwa from the Mughals in the 1720s and 1730s. The Peshwa Baji Rao I confirmed him in possession of Dhar, the old Paramara capital, making him the founder of the Puar princely house of Dhar.

anand-singh-of-idar.s: Anand Singh was a Rathore prince, brother of Maharaja Abhai Singh of Jodhpur, who with his brother Rai Singh took the fortress of Idar in north-eastern Gujarat in 1728. He founded the Rathore line that ruled Idar State until 1948.

anangapala-ii.s: Anangapala II was a king of the Tomara dynasty who ruled the Delhi region in the 11th century. He is credited with founding Lal Kot, the earliest identifiable fortified city of Delhi, and the iron pillar now at the Qutb complex is traditionally linked to him.

anapota-nayaka.s: Anapota Nayaka was a chief of the Recherla family of Velama Nayakas in Telangana. Allied with the Bahmani Sultanate, he defeated and killed Kapaya Nayaka of the Musunuri Nayaks around 1368 and established Recherla rule over much of Telangana.

anastasia-of-slutsk.s: Anastasia of Slutsk was the widow of Prince Semyon Olelkovich and ruled the Duchy of Slutsk as regent for her son Yury in the early 16th century. In 1506 she organised the defence of Slutsk against a Crimean Tatar siege, which made her a heroine of Belarusian tradition.

anastasio-bustamante.s: Anastasio Bustamante was a Mexican general and conservative politician who served as president of Mexico three times between 1830 and 1841. His second term fell in the centralist period, when Mexico faced the Texas Revolution, the French blockade of the Pastry War and…

anatolijs-gorbunovs.s: Anatolijs Gorbunovs is a Latvian politician who chaired the Supreme Council of the Latvian SSR from 1988. Under his chairmanship the council declared the restoration of Latvia's independence on 4 May 1990, completed on 21 August 1991.

anatoly-stessel.s: Anatoly Stessel was a Russian general who commanded at Port Arthur during the Russo-Japanese War. After a siege of more than five months he surrendered the fortress to the Japanese in January 1905, while it still had men and supplies.

anaxilas.s: Anaxilas was tyrant of Rhegion on the toe of Italy in the early 5th century BCE. He seized Zancle across the strait, settled it with Messenians and renamed it Messana, giving him control of both shores of the Strait of Messina.

andi-djemma.s: Andi Djemma was the datu, or king, of Luwu in South Sulawesi from 1935. He declared Luwu's support for the Indonesian Republic in 1945 and led resistance to the returning Dutch until his capture in 1946.

andrea-ii-muzaka.s: Andrea II Muzaka was an Albanian noble of the Muzaka family, whose lands lay in the Myzeqe plain and around Berat. Around 1335 he received the Byzantine title of despot for fighting the Angevins, and he built the family's lordship into one of the leading noble realms of late…

andreas-joseph-hofmann.s: Andreas Joseph Hofmann was a German philosopher and professor at the University of Mainz who supported the French Revolution. In March 1793 he presided over the Rhenish-German National Convention, which proclaimed the Republic of Mainz, the first republic on German soil.

andreas-papandreou.s: Andreas Papandreou was a Greek economist and politician who founded the Panhellenic Socialist Movement (PASOK) in 1974, after the fall of the military junta. He was prime minister from 1981 to 1989 and again from 1993 to 1996, expanding the welfare state.

andregoto-galindez.s: Andregoto Galíndez was the heiress of the County of Aragon, daughter of Count Galindo Aznárez II. Her marriage to García Sánchez I of Pamplona in the 920s or 930s brought Aragon under the Navarrese crown.

andres-bonifacio.s: Andrés Bonifacio was a Filipino revolutionary who co-founded the Katipunan secret society in Manila in 1892 and became its supreme leader. He launched the Philippine Revolution against Spain in August 1896.

andrew-iii-of-hungary.s: Andrew III was king of Hungary from 1290 and the last male member of the Árpád dynasty. His reign was marked by the growing power of barons such as Matthew Csák, who built regional domains as royal authority weakened.

andries-waterboer.s: Andries Waterboer was a Griqua leader who became kaptein at Griquatown in 1820. In 1834 he made a treaty with the Cape Colony that brought him a subsidy and arms in return for guarding the frontier.

andriy-brodiy.s: Andriy Brodiy was a Rusyn politician who became the first prime minister of autonomous Subcarpathian Ruthenia in October 1938. He was soon arrested by the Czechoslovak authorities for pro-Hungarian activity and replaced by Avgustyn Voloshyn.

andronikos-asen.s: Andronikos Asen was a Byzantine aristocrat of Bulgarian royal descent who served as governor of the Byzantine province of the Morea. In 1320 he captured Karytaina, Akova and other castles in the centre of the Peloponnese from the Principality of Achaea, ending Frankish rule…

andronikos-asen-zaccaria.s: Andronikos Asen Zaccaria was a Genoese noble of the Zaccaria family who held the barony of Arcadia (Kyparissia) in the Principality of Achaea in the late 14th century. His son Centurione II Zaccaria became Prince of Achaea in 1404 and fell back on Arcadia as the Byzantines…

andronikos-ii-palaiologos.s: Andronikos II Palaiologos was Byzantine emperor from 1282 to 1328. His long reign saw the loss of most of Anatolia to the Turks and the ravages of the Catalan Company, which he had hired.

ang-duong.s: Ang Duong was king of Cambodia, installed in the 1840s after a war between Siam and Vietnam over the country and crowned in 1848. He restored Buddhist institutions and administration and sought French help to escape Siamese and Vietnamese domination.

anglo-french-convention-of-1898.s: The Anglo-French Convention of 1898 was an agreement signed in Paris on 14 June 1898 that settled the frontier between British and French territories in West Africa, especially along the Niger. It assigned Bussa to Britain, which became part of Northern Nigeria, and Nikki to…

anglo-nepalese-war.s: The Anglo-Nepalese War was fought between the East India Company and the Kingdom of Nepal. It ended with the Treaty of Sugauli, by which Nepal gave up Kumaon, Garhwal and the hill country between the Sutlej and the Kali.

anglo-persian-oil-company.s: The Anglo-Persian Oil Company was a British company founded in 1909 to exploit oil discovered at Masjed Soleyman in south-western Iran, on Bakhtiari land. It built a refinery on Abadan island, leased from Sheikh Khazal of Mohammerah, and the British government became its…

aniceto-lacson.s: Aniceto Lacson was a sugar planter of Negros who, with Juan Araneta, led the rising of 5 November 1898 against the Spanish garrison on the island. He became president of the Republic of Negros, which soon sought American protection.

anirudh-chand.s: Anirudh Chand was the son of Sansar Chand and the last raja of Kangra in the Himalayan foothills. In 1828 he fled to British territory rather than marry his sisters into the family of the Sikh minister Dhian Singh, and Ranjit Singh annexed his lands.

anitta.s: Anitta was a king of Kussara in central Anatolia and son of Pithana, who had taken the city of Nesa (Kanesh). He conquered Zalpa and Hattus, cursed the latter, and received the submission of the great king of Purushanda.

annama-deva.s: Annama Deva is the traditional founder of the Kakatiya royal line of Bastar in central India. According to tradition he was a brother of the last Kakatiya king Prataparudra and fled north after the Delhi Sultanate took Warangal in 1323.

anne-of-brittany.s: Anne of Brittany was duchess of Brittany from 1488 and twice queen of France, through marriage to Charles VIII in 1491 and Louis XII in 1499. She worked to preserve the duchy's separate status.

anne-of-cleves.s: Anne of Cleves was a daughter of Duke John III of Cleves and the fourth wife of Henry VIII of England. The marriage, arranged in 1540 to ally England with the Protestant-leaning princes of the lower Rhine, was annulled after six months.

anne-of-forez.s: Anne of Forez was the heiress of the County of Forez in central France. Her marriage to Louis II, Duke of Bourbon, in 1371 brought Forez into the Bourbon lands.

ansa-sasraku.s: Ansa Sasraku was a king of Akwamu, an Akan state in the hinterland of the Gold Coast. Between 1677 and 1681 he conquered the Ga kingdom around Accra, giving Akwamu access to the European forts on the coast and control of the trade in gold and slaves.

anselm-erb.s: Anselm Erb was abbot of the Benedictine Imperial Abbey of Ottobeuren in Swabia from 1740 until his death. Under him the great abbey church was built and completed in 1766 to designs by Johann Michael Fischer, one of the masterpieces of south German Rococo.

antanas-snieckus.s: Antanas Sniečkus was first secretary of the Communist Party of Lithuania from 1940 until his death in 1974, the longest-serving party leader in Soviet Lithuania. He oversaw the Soviet annexation, the deportations of the 1940s and the struggle against the armed resistance, but…

ante-pavelic.s: Ante Pavelić was the founder of the fascist Ustaše movement and leader, as Poglavnik, of the Independent State of Croatia from 1941 to 1945. His regime, an Axis puppet state, carried out genocide against Serbs, Jews and Roma, including at the Jasenovac camp.

anthony-hilton.s: Anthony Hilton was an English planter who led settlers from Saint Kitts to found the first English settlement on Nevis in 1628. He served as the island's first governor.

antigonus-ii-gonatas.s: Antigonus II Gonatas was king of Macedon and son of Demetrius Poliorcetes. His victory over the Gauls at Lysimachia in 277 BCE won him the Macedonian throne, and he established the Antigonid dynasty firmly in Macedon.

antigonus-iii-doson.s: Antigonus III Doson was king of Macedon from 229 BCE. Called in by the Achaean League against Cleomenes III of Sparta, he took cities in Arcadia, including Orchomenus and Mantinea in 223 BCE, and defeated Cleomenes at Sellasia in 222 BCE.

antipater.s: Antipater was a Macedonian general and statesman who served Philip II and governed Macedon and Greece while Alexander the Great campaigned in Asia. After Alexander's death he defeated Athens and its allies in the Lamian War at Crannon in 322 BCE.

antoine-iii-de-gramont.s: Antoine III de Gramont was a French noble, sovereign lord of Bidache and Marshal of France from 1641. He served as a commander in the Thirty Years' War and as a diplomat under Louis XIV, negotiating the king's marriage to Maria Theresa of Spain.

antoine-lefebvre-de-la-barre.s: Antoine Lefebvre de La Barre was a French colonial administrator who established a lasting French settlement at Cayenne in French Guiana in 1664. He later commanded French forces in the Caribbean and served as governor of New France from 1682 to 1685, where his failed campaign…

antoine-of-vaudemont.s: Antoine of Vaudémont was count of Vaudémont and a member of the house of Lorraine. He claimed the Duchy of Lorraine against René of Anjou and defeated and captured him at Bulgnéville in 1431.

anton-holovaty.s: Anton Holovaty was a Cossack officer of the former Zaporozhian Host who helped form the Black Sea Cossack Host under Russian rule. He fought at Ochakiv and Izmail in the Russo-Turkish War of 1787–1792 and negotiated the host's resettlement in the Kuban in 1792.

anton-korosec.s: Anton Korošec was a Slovene Catholic priest and politician who presided over the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs proclaimed in October 1918. He led the Slovene People's Party for two decades and served in many governments of the Kingdom of Yugoslavia, becoming its only…

anton-lutskevich.s: Anton Lutskevich was a Belarusian politician and publicist, a founder of the Belarusian national movement. He led the government of the Belarusian People's Republic from 1918 to 1920 and sought international recognition for it.

anton-slutsky.s: Anton Slutsky was a Bolshevik who became chairman of the council of people's commissars of the Soviet Socialist Republic of Taurida, proclaimed in Crimea in March 1918. When German troops advanced and a Crimean Tatar revolt broke out in April 1918, he and other leaders were…

antonin-janousek.s: Antonín Janoušek was a Czech communist who headed the Slovak Soviet Republic, proclaimed at Prešov in June 1919 with the support of the Hungarian Soviet Republic. After the republic collapsed in July 1919 he fled to Hungary and later the Soviet Union.

antonine-wall.s: The Antonine Wall was a Roman turf rampart built across the Forth–Clyde isthmus of central Scotland from 142 on the orders of Emperor Antoninus Pius. It marked the northern frontier of Roman Britain for about twenty years before the army withdrew to Hadrian's Wall.

antonio-canales-rosillo.s: Antonio Canales Rosillo was a Mexican lawyer and federalist soldier from Tamaulipas. In 1840 he became commander of the army of the Republic of the Rio Grande, the federalist breakaway state of northern Mexico, and later came to terms with the centralist government.

antonio-canovas-del-castillo.s: Antonio Cánovas del Castillo was a Spanish conservative statesman and historian who designed the Bourbon Restoration of 1874 and its Constitution of 1876. He led the Conservative Party and created the turno pacífico, under which Conservatives and Liberals alternated in power.

antonio-carreno-de-valdes.s: Antonio Carreño de Valdés was a Spanish officer who led the expedition from Manila to northern Taiwan in 1626. His force occupied the harbour of Keelung, founding the settlement of Santísima Trinidad and Fort San Salvador to counter the Dutch in the south of the island.

antonio-coelho-guerreiro.s: António Coelho Guerreiro was a Portuguese administrator who arrived at Lifau in 1702 as the first governor appointed for Timor and Solor. His arrival marked the start of formal Portuguese government on the island, though authority there remained long contested by the Topasses,…

antonio-correia.s: António Correia was a Portuguese commander who led a Portuguese and Hormuzi force against Bahrain in 1521. His victory over the Jabrid ruler Muqrin ibn Zamil, who died of his wounds, brought Bahrain under Portuguese and Hormuzi control, which lasted until the Safavids took the…

antonio-de-berrio.s: Antonio de Berrío was a Spanish conquistador and governor who devoted his last years to the search for El Dorado on the Orinoco. In 1592 he founded San José de Oruña on Trinidad as a base for his expeditions.

antonio-de-mendoza.s: Antonio de Mendoza was a Castilian noble who became the first viceroy of New Spain in 1535. He set up the viceregal administration in Mexico City, founded the first mint in the Americas and encouraged printing and education.

antonio-de-noli.s: Antonio de Noli was a Genoese navigator in Portuguese service who was among the discoverers of the Cape Verde islands around 1460. He became captain of the southern part of Santiago, where Ribeira Grande, today's Cidade Velha, grew into one of the first European towns in the…

antonio-de-sousa-neto.s: Antônio de Sousa Neto was a gaúcho general of the Ragamuffin War in southern Brazil. After his victory at Seival on 10 September 1836 he proclaimed the Riograndense Republic the next day.

antonio-galvez-arce.s: Antonio Gálvez Arce, known as Antoñete, was a Spanish federalist politician from Murcia. On 12 July 1873 he led the proclamation of the Canton of Cartagena, the most durable of the cantonal revolts against the First Spanish Republic.

antonio-narino.s: Antonio Nariño was a New Granadan revolutionary who translated and printed the Declaration of the Rights of Man in 1794 and was imprisoned for it. He became president of the Free and Independent State of Cundinamarca in 1811 and led its centralist cause against the federalist…

antonio-pigafetta.s: Antonio Pigafetta was a Venetian scholar who sailed with Ferdinand Magellan in 1519 and was one of the few survivors of the first circumnavigation of the world. His account of the voyage is the main source for the expedition and describes the peoples it met, including the…

antonio-rolim-de-moura.s: Antônio Rolim de Moura was a Portuguese nobleman and the first governor of the Captaincy of Mato Grosso in western Brazil. In 1752 he founded its capital, Vila Bela da Santíssima Trindade, on the Guaporé river to secure the frontier with Spanish America.

antony-bek.s: Antony Bek was bishop of Durham from 1284 and a leading servant of Edward I of England. He took part in the king's Scottish campaigns, including the Battle of Falkirk in 1298, and was made titular patriarch of Jerusalem in 1306.

anwar-ibrahim.s: Anwar Ibrahim is a Malaysian politician who was deputy prime minister under Mahathir Mohamad until his dismissal and imprisonment in 1998. He led the reform movement and opposition coalition for more than two decades and became prime minister of Malaysia in November 2022.

anwar-sadat.s: Anwar Sadat was president of Egypt from 1970 until his assassination in 1981. He launched the October War of 1973 against Israel, opened the economy and turned Egypt from the Soviet Union towards the United States.

apollo-delphinios.s: Apollo Delphinios was a form of the Greek god Apollo, linked to dolphins, the sea and the founding of colonies. His cult was especially strong in Miletus and the cities it founded around the Black Sea, such as Olbia, and was also a chief cult at Massalia.

aq-sunqur-ii.s: Aq Sunqur II was an atabeg of the Ahmadili dynasty that ruled Maragheh in Azerbaijan in the 12th century. Like his father Aq Sunqur I, he supported rival princes of the Seljuk Sultanate of Iraq against the Eldiguzids, the dynasty's main rivals in north-western Iran.

aquae-tarbellicae.s: Aquae Tarbellicae was the Roman town on the site of Dax in south-western France, chief town of the Tarbelli people. Its hot springs became famous under Rome, and under Augustus it became the centre of the Tarbelli civitas.

arauco-war.s: The Arauco War was the long conflict between the Spanish and the Mapuche of south-central Chile. It began with the Spanish invasion of the 1540s; the Mapuche killed Pedro de Valdivia at Tucapel in 1553 and destroyed the southern Spanish towns after Curalaba in 1598.

archduke-rainer-joseph-of-austria.s: Archduke Rainer Joseph was a son of Emperor Leopold II and brother of Francis I of Austria. He served as viceroy of the Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia from 1818 to 1848, residing mainly in Milan, and presided over its efficient but unpopular administration until the revolutions…

ardo-njobdi.s: Ardo Njobdi was a Fulbe leader who founded Ngaoundere around 1835 under the authority of the Adamawa Emirate. His forces conquered the Mbum people of the Adamawa plateau in present-day Cameroon.

arduin-glaber.s: Arduin Glaber was a 10th-century count who received control of Turin and the Susa valley around 941 and founded the March of Turin. He drove the Saracens of Fraxinetum from the Alpine passes.

arechis-ii-of-benevento.s: Arechis II was duke of Benevento from 758. When Charlemagne conquered the Lombard kingdom in 774, he took the title of prince, claiming to carry on the Lombard tradition in southern Italy.

aretas-iii.s: Aretas III was king of the Nabataeans who extended his kingdom north and took Damascus around 85 BCE, ruling it for several years. He intervened in the Hasmonean civil war in Judaea and was forced to withdraw by the Roman general Scaurus, to whom he later paid tribute.

aretas-iv.s: Aretas IV was king of the Nabataeans, whose long reign marked the height of Petra's prosperity and building. His daughter married Herod Antipas, tetrarch of Galilee, who divorced her to marry Herodias; Aretas defeated Antipas in a war in 36 CE.

ari-malla.s: Ari Malla was the first king of the Kathmandu Valley to bear the Malla title, beginning the Malla period of Nepalese history around 1200. The dynasty he began ruled the valley until the Gorkha conquest of 1768 to 1769, shaping Newar culture, art and architecture.

arianism.s: Arianism was a Christian doctrine, named after the Alexandrian priest Arius, holding that the Son was created by the Father and not of the same substance. Condemned at the Council of Nicaea in 325, it spread among the Goths, Vandals, Rugians and other Germanic peoples, setting…

arikesari-ii.s: Arikesari II was a ruler of the Chalukyas of Vemulavada in present-day Telangana, feudatories of the Rashtrakutas. He is remembered as the patron of the poet Pampa, whose Kannada epics Vikramarjuna Vijaya and Adipurana were written at his court around 941 and celebrate him…

arikesari-maravarman.s: Arikesari Maravarman was a king of the early medieval Pandya dynasty of Madurai in the later 7th century. Shaiva tradition holds that the saint Sambandar converted him from Jainism to Shaivism, an episode associated with the rise of the Bhakti movement in Tamil country.

arikesari-parakrama-pandya.s: Arikesari Parakrama Pandya was a ruler of the later Pandya line settled at Tenkasi in the Tirunelveli region. In the 1440s he began the great Kasi Viswanathar temple at Tenkasi, the chief monument of the Tenkasi Pandyas, who ruled as subordinates of larger southern powers.

arima-toyouji.s: Arima Toyouji was a Japanese daimyo who fought for Tokugawa Ieyasu at Sekigahara in 1600. In 1621 the shogunate gave him Kurume in Chikugo province, with about 210,000 koku, and his descendants ruled the Kurume Domain until 1871.

arima-yoriyuki.s: Arima Yoriyuki was daimyo of the Kurume Domain in Kyushu and a noted mathematician of the Japanese wasan tradition. He published works on mathematics, including the Shuki Sanpo of 1769.

aristagoras-of-miletus.s: Aristagoras was tyrant of Miletus, ruling in place of his father-in-law Histiaeus under Persian authority. After a failed expedition against Naxos he led the Ionian cities into the Ionian Revolt against Persia in 499 BCE and sought help from Sparta and Athens.

aristagoras-of-cyme.s: Aristagoras of Cyme was a tyrant of the Aeolian city of Cyme under Persian rule. Herodotus lists him among the Greek tyrants who guarded Darius I's bridge over the Danube during the Scythian campaign of about 513 BCE.

arjun-pal.s: Arjun Pal was a Jadaun Rajput chief who founded the town of Karauli in eastern Rajasthan in 1348. Karauli became the capital of the state ruled by his Jadaun descendants, who claimed descent from the Yadavas, until it joined the Matsya Union in 1948.

armand-bouchart.s: Armand Bouchart was a Knight Templar who governed Cyprus for the order after the Templars bought the island from Richard I of England in 1191. His small garrison imposed heavy taxes, provoking a rising in Nicosia in April 1192.

armed-forces-movement.s: The Armed Forces Movement was an organisation of junior Portuguese officers, weary of the colonial wars in Africa, that overthrew the Estado Novo regime on 25 April 1974 in the Carnation Revolution. It steered the transition to democracy and the decolonisation of Portugal's…

armenian-revolutionary-federation.s: The Armenian Revolutionary Federation, or Dashnaktsutyun, is an Armenian nationalist and socialist party founded in Tiflis in 1890. In 1917 and 1918 its members took part in the Transcaucasian governments and its armed units fought in Baku and Central Asia; it then led the…

armenian-oblast.s: The Armenian Oblast was a province of the Russian Empire formed in 1828 from the Erivan and Nakhichevan khanates ceded by Qajar Iran in the Treaty of Turkmenchay. Many Armenians from Iran resettled there.

arnold-of-brescia.s: Arnold of Brescia was an Italian canon and reformer who preached against the wealth and temporal power of the clergy. From 1145 he supported the Commune of Rome against the papacy.

arpad.s: Árpád was the leader of the Hungarian tribal federation who, after his father Álmos, led the Hungarians across the Carpathians into the Carpathian Basin around 895. He is regarded as the founder of the Árpád dynasty, which ruled Hungary as princes and then kings until 1301.

arpad-goncz.s: Árpád Göncz was a Hungarian writer, translator and politician who was imprisoned after the 1956 revolution. In 1990 he became the first president of the Third Hungarian Republic, serving two terms until 2000.

artavasdes-ii-of-armenia.s: Artavasdes II was king of Armenia from about 55 BCE, son of Tigranes the Great. He balanced between Rome and Parthia, and was blamed by Mark Antony for the failure of his Parthian campaign of 36 BCE.

artaxias-iv.s: Artaxias IV was the last Arsacid king of Armenia, ruling the Sasanian-controlled part of the country. In 428 the Armenian nobles asked the Persian king Bahram V to depose him, and the Armenian monarchy was abolished.

artemisia-ii-of-caria.s: Artemisia II was the sister and wife of Mausolus of Caria and ruled after his death in 353 BCE. She completed his tomb at Halicarnassus, the Mausoleum, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, and is said to have captured Rhodes.

arthur-cipriani.s: Arthur Cipriani was a Trinidadian soldier, labour leader and politician of Corsican descent. After serving in the First World War, he led the Trinidad Workingmen's Association from 1923 and campaigned for self-government, workers' rights and universal suffrage.

arthur-macarthur-jr.s: Arthur MacArthur Jr. was an American general who served as military governor of the Philippines in 1900 and 1901, during the Philippine–American War. His forces captured Emilio Aguinaldo in March 1901, and he handed over civil authority to William Howard Taft.

arthur-phillip.s: Arthur Phillip was a Royal Navy officer who commanded the First Fleet of convict ships to Australia. He founded the settlement at Sydney Cove in January 1788 and served as the first governor of New South Wales until 1792, guiding the colony through its early food shortages.

artur-gorgei.s: Artúr Görgei was the leading Hungarian general of the revolution of 1848–1849. His spring campaign of 1849 drove the Austrians back and recaptured Buda in May.

arung-palakka.s: Arung Palakka was a Bugis prince of Bone in South Sulawesi who allied with the Dutch East India Company against the Gowa Sultanate. With Cornelis Speelman he defeated Gowa between 1666 and 1669, leading to the Treaty of Bongaya.

arvids-pelse.s: Arvīds Pelše was a Latvian communist who was first secretary of the Communist Party of Latvia from 1959 to 1966. He led the purge of the Latvian national communists in 1959 and promoted Russification and industrial growth.

arya-wiraraja.s: Arya Wiraraja was a Javanese noble appointed adipati of Sumenep in eastern Madura by Kertanegara of Singhasari, traditionally in 1269. According to the chronicles he advised Jayakatwang and then helped Raden Wijaya defeat him and found Majapahit in 1293.

asad-ibn-ibrahim.s: As'ad ibn Ibrahim was a ruler of the Yufirid dynasty of the Yemeni highlands. In the early 10th century he recovered Sanaa from the Isma'ili missionary Ali ibn al-Fadl and dominated highland politics for several decades.

asakura-toshikage.s: Asakura Toshikage was a Japanese warrior who used the Ōnin War to seize control of Echizen province from his former lords, the Shiba. He made Ichijōdani the seat of the Asakura and is known for a set of house rules for his family, one of the earliest codes of a sengoku daimyo.

asakura-yoshikage.s: Asakura Yoshikage was the last Asakura lord of Echizen. He sheltered the future shogun Ashikaga Yoshiaki and allied with the Azai against Oda Nobunaga, sharing their defeat at Anegawa in 1570.

asano-nagaakira.s: Asano Nagaakira was a Japanese daimyo, son of Asano Nagamasa. In 1619 the shogunate transferred him to Hiroshima, with about 426,000 koku, after the dismissal of Fukushima Masanori.

ashikaga-mochiuji.s: Ashikaga Mochiuji was the Kamakura kubo, the shogun's deputy for the Kanto, from 1409. He survived the Uesugi Zenshū revolt of 1416 but came into open conflict with Shogun Ashikaga Yoshinori.

ashikaga-shigeuji.s: Ashikaga Shigeuji was the son of Ashikaga Mochiuji and was restored as Kamakura kubo in 1449. In 1454 he had the Kanto deputy Uesugi Noritada killed, starting the long Kyōtoku War.

ashikaga-yoshiuji.s: Ashikaga Yoshiuji was the last Koga kubo, son of Ashikaga Haruuji and a Hōjō mother. He held the title under the control of the Later Hōjō clan.

ashot-iii-of-armenia.s: Ashot III, called the Merciful, was king of Bagratid Armenia. In 961 he moved the capital to Ani, which grew into a great city on the trade routes between Byzantium and Iran.

ashot-msaker.s: Ashot Msaker, the Carnivore, was a Bagratid prince who became presiding prince of Armenia under the Abbasid Caliphate in the early 9th century. He built up the family's lands, which were divided among his sons; one son, Bagrat, received Taron, founding its line of princes.

ashraf-ghani.s: Ashraf Ghani is an Afghan academic and politician who served as president of the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan from 2014 to 2021, at first sharing power with Abdullah Abdullah. As the Taliban took the country following the US withdrawal, he fled Kabul on 15 August 2021, and…

askia-nuh.s: Askia Nuh was a prince of the Songhai Empire who led its resistance after the Moroccan victory at Tondibi in 1591. He withdrew down the Niger into Dendi, in present-day south-western Niger, where he fought a guerrilla war against the Moroccans and founded the line of askias…

assizes-of-romania.s: The Assizes of Romania is a code of feudal law compiled in the Principality of Achaea in the first half of the 14th century. It recorded the customs governing the prince, barons and vassals of Frankish Greece and was later adopted in Venetian possessions in the Aegean.

assur-fernandez.s: Assur Fernández was a Castilian noble whom Ramiro II of León made count of Monzón, near Palencia, around 943. The county was created as a counterweight to Fernán González of Castile.

astorre-iii-manfredi.s: Astorre III Manfredi was the last Manfredi lord of Faenza in Romagna. When Cesare Borgia besieged Faenza in 1501, the city surrendered on terms, but the young lord was taken to Rome, imprisoned in Castel Sant'Angelo and murdered in 1502.

asturica-augusta.s: Asturica Augusta was the Roman town on the site of Astorga in north-western Spain, founded after Augustus' Cantabrian Wars in the land of the Astures. It became the administrative centre of the gold-mining district that included Las Médulas and an important road junction.

atamu-tekena.s: Atamu Tekena was ariki, or king, of Rapa Nui (Easter Island) in the late 19th century. On 9 September 1888 he signed the agreement with the Chilean naval captain Policarpo Toro by which Chile annexed the island.

athanasios-the-athonite.s: Athanasios the Athonite was a Byzantine monk who founded the Great Lavra on Mount Athos in 963 with the support of his friend Nikephoros Phokas, later emperor. It was the first large organised monastery on the peninsula, and his rules shaped Athonite monasticism.

ativira-rama-pandya.s: Ativira Rama Pandya was a ruler of the later Pandya line at Tenkasi in the 16th century, subordinate to the Vijayanagara Empire and the Madurai Nayaks. He is remembered as a Tamil poet, author of the Naidatham, a Tamil version of the story of Nala and Damayanti.

atsiz-ibn-uvaq.s: Atsiz ibn Uvaq was a Turkmen commander who took Jerusalem from the Fatimids in 1073 and Damascus in 1076, founding the first Turkish state in Syria and Palestine. After a failed invasion of Egypt in 1077 he called for help from the Seljuks; the sultan's brother Tutush had him…

attalus-iii.s: Attalus III was the last Attalid king of Pergamon, reigning from 138 BCE. On his death in 133 BCE he left his kingdom to Rome in his will.

au-viet.s: The Âu Việt were an ancient people of the northern uplands of present-day Vietnam and southern China. According to Vietnamese tradition, their leader Thục Phán overthrew the last Hùng king of Văn Lang around 258 BCE and united the Âu Việt and Lạc Việt in the kingdom of Âu Lạc.

augusto-pinochet.s: Augusto Pinochet was a Chilean general who led the military coup of 11 September 1973 that overthrew Salvador Allende. He ruled Chile as dictator until 1990, with widespread repression and free-market economic reforms, and imposed the constitution of 1980.

augustus-duke-of-saxe-weissenfels.s: Augustus was a son of Elector John George I of Saxony and administrator of the Archbishopric of Magdeburg. Under his father's will he received Weissenfels, Querfurt and other lands in 1656, founding the Duchy of Saxe-Weissenfels.

augustus-the-younger-duke-of-brunswick-l.n: Augustus the Younger, Duke of Brunswick-Lüneburg
augustus-the-younger-duke-of-brunswick-l.s: Augustus the Younger was Duke of Brunswick-Lüneburg who ruled the Principality of Wolfenbüttel from 1635 until his death in 1666. A scholar and passionate collector, he built up the ducal library at Wolfenbüttel, which by his death was among the largest in Europe and is now…

aulus-plautius.s: Aulus Plautius was a Roman senator and general who commanded the invasion of Britain ordered by the emperor Claudius in 43 CE. Leading four legions, he defeated the Catuvellauni, took Camulodunum with the emperor present, and accepted the surrender of peoples such as part of…

aurelio-saffi.s: Aurelio Saffi was an Italian republican politician from Forlì and a close follower of Giuseppe Mazzini. In 1849 he served with Mazzini and Carlo Armellini as one of the three triumvirs who governed the short-lived Roman Republic until French troops restored papal rule.

ausias-march.s: Ausiàs March was a Valencian knight and poet, the leading lyric poet of medieval Catalan literature. Breaking with the Occitan troubadour tradition that earlier Catalan poets had followed, he wrote introspective verse on love, death and faith in his own language.

avan-yuzbashi.s: Avan Yuzbashi was an Armenian military commander in Karabakh in the 1720s, when the collapse of Safavid Persia exposed the South Caucasus to Ottoman invasion. Holding the rank of yuzbashi, or captain, he led the armed forces of the Karabakh meliks against the Ottomans,…

avgustyn-voloshyn.s: Avgustyn Voloshyn was a Greek Catholic priest, teacher and Ukrainian political leader in Subcarpathian Ruthenia. After the Munich Agreement he became prime minister of the autonomous region in October 1938, moving his government to Khust, and on 15 March 1939 he was named…

ayia-triada.s: Ayia Triada is a Minoan archaeological site in southern Crete, about three kilometres west of the palace of Phaistos. Its large Bronze Age villa and settlement were closely linked to Phaistos and became the leading centre of the Mesara plain after the palace was destroyed.

ayios-vasileios.s: Ayios Vasileios is a Mycenaean palace site near Xirokambi, south of Sparta in Laconia, Greece. Excavations begun in 2010, after Linear B tablets were found there, uncovered a palace complex with courts, archives and cult rooms.

ayyanadikal-thiruvadikal.s: Ayyanadikal Thiruvadikal was the ruler of Venad in southern Kerala in the mid-ninth century, under the overlordship of the Chera Perumal king Sthanu Ravi. In the Tharisapalli copper plates of 849 he granted land, serfs and trading privileges to the Syrian Christian church of…

azai-sukemasa.s: Azai Sukemasa was a Japanese warlord of the Sengoku period who founded the power of the Azai clan in northern Ōmi province. A retainer of the Kyōgoku family, he took control of their lands during internal conflicts in the 1520s and built Odani Castle on a mountain above Lake…

absalon.s: Absalon was a Danish churchman and statesman, Bishop of Roskilde and later Archbishop of Lund, and the chief adviser of King Valdemar I. He led Danish campaigns against the pagan Wends of the Baltic coast, and in 1168 he and Valdemar stormed Arkona on Rügen and destroyed the…

aden-protectorate.s: The Aden Protectorate was the group of sultanates, emirates and sheikhdoms in southern Arabia bound to Britain by treaties of protection around the port of Aden. Its border with Ottoman Yemen was fixed between 1904 and 1914, and the imams of Yemen later claimed it.

armed-forces-of-south-russia.s: The Armed Forces of South Russia were the main White army in southern Russia during the Russian Civil War, formed in January 1919 under General Anton Denikin. Combining the Volunteer Army with the Don and Kuban Cossack forces, they advanced as far as Oryol in October 1919…

albert-duke-of-prussia.s: Albert, Duke of Prussia, a Hohenzollern of the Ansbach line, was the last Grand Master of the Teutonic Order in Prussia. In 1525, advised by Martin Luther, he converted to Lutheranism and secularised the Order's state as the Duchy of Prussia under the Polish crown, the first…

armand-emmanuel-du-plessis-duc-de-richel.n: Armand-Emmanuel du Plessis, Duc de Richelieu
armand-emmanuel-du-plessis-duc-de-richel.s: Armand-Emmanuel du Plessis, Duc de Richelieu, was a French aristocrat who served Russia during the emigration as governor of Odessa. Returning after 1814, he was prime minister of the Bourbon Restoration from 1815 to 1818 and from 1820 to 1821.

andrew-rutherford-1st-earl-of-teviot.s: Andrew Rutherford, 1st Earl of Teviot, was a Scottish soldier who served in the French army and as governor of Dunkirk before Charles II made him governor of English Tangier in 1663. He began the great mole and new defences of the port, but was killed with many of his men in…

arsenio-martinez-campos.s: Arsenio Martínez Campos was a Spanish general who suppressed the cantonal rising in Valencia in 1873 and in December 1874 proclaimed Alfonso XII king at Sagunto, restoring the Bourbon monarchy. He later ended the Ten Years' War in Cuba with the Pact of Zanjón in 1878 and…

aleksey-yermolov.s: Aleksey Yermolov was a Russian general who commanded in the Caucasus from 1816 to 1827. He built fortresses such as Grozny, broke the independence of Kabarda and defeated the Dargin communities of Akusha in 1819, using punitive raids and deportations.

adolphus-frederick-vi-grand-duke-of-meck.n: Adolphus Frederick VI, Grand Duke of Mecklenburg-Strelitz
adolphus-frederick-vi-grand-duke-of-meck.s: Adolphus Frederick VI was the last reigning Grand Duke of Mecklenburg-Strelitz, from 1914 to 1918. Unmarried, he took his own life in February 1918, leaving no direct heir and the succession disputed between distant relatives.

ahmad-ibn-fadlan.s: Ahmad ibn Fadlan was an Arab member of the embassy sent by the Abbasid caliph al-Muqtadir to the king of the Volga Bulgars in 921 to 922. His account describes the Oghuz Turks, the Bulgars' conversion to Islam and a Rus' ship burial on the Volga.

aulic-council.s: The Aulic Council, or Reichshofrat, was one of the two supreme courts of the Holy Roman Empire, alongside the Imperial Chamber Court. Sitting at the emperor's court in Vienna, it heard disputes between imperial estates and feudal cases.

abbas-ii-of-egypt.s: Abbas II Hilmi was the last Khedive of Egypt, reigning from 1892 to 1914. Succeeding his father Tewfik, he tried to resist British control exercised by Lord Cromer and gave covert support to Egyptian nationalists.

alboin.s: Alboin was king of the Lombards from about 560 and led them out of Pannonia into Italy in 568, soon after the Gothic Wars had exhausted the peninsula. He conquered much of northern Italy, took Pavia after a long siege and set up the first Lombard duchy at Cividale under his…

ahmad-nizam-shah-i.s: Ahmad Nizam Shah I was the founder of the Nizam Shahi dynasty and the Ahmadnagar Sultanate in the Deccan. The son of a Bahmani minister, he defeated a Bahmani army in 1490 and declared his independence, one of the breakaways that ended the Bahmani Sultanate.

auguste-de-marmont.s: Auguste de Marmont was a French general and Marshal of the Empire under Napoleon. As commander in Dalmatia he abolished the Republic of Poljica in 1807 and the Republic of Ragusa in 1808, receiving the title Duke of Ragusa, and governed the Illyrian Provinces from 1809 to 1811.

al-muayyad-muhammad.s: Al-Mu'ayyad Muhammad was the Zaydi imam of Yemen from 1620 to 1644 and the second ruler of the Qasimid State. Continuing the revolt begun by his father al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, he drove the Ottomans from the highlands, took Sanaa and forced them to evacuate Yemen in 1636.

al-mughith-umar.s: Al-Mughith Umar was the last Ayyubid ruler of Kerak, in Transjordan, from 1250 to 1263. A grandson of Sultan al-Kamil, he made the fortress a refuge for Mamluk dissidents and twice tried to invade Egypt against the new Mamluk regime.

al-mundhir-iii.s: Al-Mundhir III ibn al-Nu'man was the most powerful king of the Lakhmids of al-Hira, Arab clients of Sasanian Persia, ruling from about 503 to 554. He raided Roman Syria repeatedly and was a major figure in the wars between Persia and Byzantium.

al-mutadid-of-seville.s: Abbad II al-Mu'tadid was the second Abbadid ruler of the Taifa of Seville, reigning from 1042 to 1069. Ruthless and ambitious, he made Seville the strongest taifa of western al-Andalus by absorbing smaller neighbours, among them Huelva in 1051 and Silves in 1063.

al-salt-ibn-malik.s: Al-Salt ibn Malik was Ibadi imam of Oman from 851 to 886, one of the longest-reigning rulers of the first imamate. His rule saw Oman prosper from Gulf trade through Sohar and from farming watered by falaj channels, and he sent a fleet to defend Socotra.

ali-qoli-khan-bakhtiari.s: Ali-Qoli Khan Bakhtiari, known as Sardar As'ad II, was a chief of the Bakhtiari tribes of south-western Iran and a supporter of the Constitutional Revolution. In 1909 he and Samsam al-Saltaneh led Bakhtiari forces to Tehran, deposed Mohammad Ali Shah and restored the…

ahmad-alaq.s: Ahmad Alaq, also called Sultan Ahmad Khan, was a Chagatai khan of the eastern part of Moghulistan from 1487, a son of Yunus Khan, ruling from Turpan. He fought the Oirats and the Ming over Hami, and went west to aid his brother against the Uzbek Shaybani Khan, dying in 1504.

abd-allah-ibn-yahya-al-kindi.s: Abd Allah ibn Yahya al-Kindi (died 748), known as Talib al-Haqq, 'seeker of truth', was a judge in Hadramawt who in 746 was proclaimed imam by Ibadi missionaries from Basra. He seized Sanaa and most of Yemen, and his forces under Abu Hamza took Mecca and Medina in 747.

andhra-mahabharatam.s: The Andhra Mahabharatam is the Telugu version of the Mahabharata, written by three poets known as the Kavitrayam. Nannaya began it in the 11th century at the court of the Eastern Chalukya king Rajaraja Narendra, Tikkana continued it in the 13th century, and Errana completed it…

an-duong-vuong.s: An Dương Vương, born Thục Phán, was according to Vietnamese tradition the ruler who overthrew the last Hùng king of Văn Lang around 257 BCE and united the Âu Việt and Lạc Việt in the kingdom of Âu Lạc. He built the spiral citadel of Cổ Loa near Hanoi and lost his kingdom to…

abu-said-mirza.s: Abu Sa'id Mirza (1424–1469) was a Timurid ruler, a great-grandson of Timur, who seized Samarkand in 1451 with the help of the Uzbek khan Abu'l-Khayr and later took Herat, reuniting much of the Timurid realm. In 1469 he invaded western Iran but was defeated and captured by Uzun…
